act_def.lift: pick an object up and keep it raised or held (holding is the goal, not a means)
act_def.place: put an object on a surface or at a location (on, next to, at a target region)
act_def.place-in: put an object into a container, receptacle, drawer, cabinet, appliance, basket
act_def.stack: put an object on top of another movable object to build a stack
act_def.handover: pass an object from one hand or arm to the other
act_def.regrasp: change how an object is held, or reorient it within the hand
act_def.insert: fit an object into a hole, slot, socket, sleeve or ring with clearance
act_def.attach: join two parts so they stay together: mount, snap, hang on a hook, cover, assemble
act_def.detach: separate joined or interlocked parts: unplug, unhook, remove a lid that is not hinged, free a puzzle piece
act_def.screw: turn a part about its axis to fasten or unfasten it: screw cap, bolt, nut, bulb
act_def.open: open a hinged or sliding mechanism: door, drawer, hinged lid, window, flap
act_def.close: close a hinged or sliding mechanism
act_def.turn: rotate a knob, dial, crank, valve, faucet handle, key or rotary layer to a setting
act_def.press: press a button, switch, lever, trigger, plunger or key
act_def.push: move an object without grasping it: push, slide, nudge, sweep it along a surface
act_def.pull: drag or pull an object or a free end towards the robot
act_def.flip: turn an object over or upright, tip or roll it
act_def.fold: fold, unfold, flatten, crease or spread cloth, paper or another sheet
act_def.thread: route a rope, cable, wire or fibre through, around or along something; tie or wrap
act_def.pour: pour liquid or granular material from one container into another or out
act_def.scoop: scoop, ladle or spoon material up and transfer it
act_def.cut: cut, slice, dice, peel or chop with a blade
act_def.wipe: wipe, scrub, brush, sweep or dust a surface to clean it
act_def.draw: draw, write, paint or stamp marks on a surface
act_def.cook: change an object's state with an appliance or heat source: cook, heat, freeze, wash, charge, inflate (the operation of the appliance itself is open/press/turn)
act_def.throw: throw, toss, launch or shoot an object so it flies free
act_def.catch: catch, trap or intercept a moving object
act_def.strike: hit, kick, bat, swing at or volley a moving or resting ball, puck or shuttle
act_def.navigate: move the base or body to another place in the scene (room, counter, region); not small adjustments
act_def.locomote: walk, run, climb, crawl or fly along a course where the gait or flight itself is the difficulty
act_def.jump: jump, hop, leap, vault or flip the whole body
act_def.balance: get to or keep a body posture: stand up, stay upright, sit, keep balance under a disturbance
act_def.reach: bring the hand, tool or body to a target pose or point where reaching it is the goal
act_def.hold: keep a reached state still for a required time: hold a pose, keep a contact, keep an object steady
act_def.search: find something that is not in view at the start: look around, open to look, explore
act_def.inspect: check, identify, count, measure or read something, or judge whether acting is safe
act_def.communicate: tell, ask, report to or decline a person (the operator)

mod.precision: tight tolerance or fine alignment decides this step
mod.force: a force or pressure must be controlled (not just reached)
mod.dynamic: the object or target moves during the step, or timing decides it
mod.deformable: the object handled in this step is deformable, a liquid or granular
mod.tool: the robot does this step through a held tool
mod.bimanual: this step needs both hands or arms acting together
mod.hidden: the object or target is not visible when the step starts
mod.constraint: the step must respect an explicit rule: keep upright, no contact, order, a forbidden region

vlabench/select_chemistry_tube_spatial.tldr: A Franka Panda arm must take out the test tube in the first row and fifth column of a rack of tubes. The tube is given only by its position in the grid, so the arm has to work out which one is meant and then pull it out of the stand without disturbing its neighbours.
steps: find the tube in row 1, column 5
out of the rack without disturbing its neighbours

why.perception: tube fixed by its grid position (1st row, 5th column) among five
why.transport: take the tube out of the stand [goal concerns where one object ends up: take the tube out of the stand]

vlabench/select_mahjong_spatial.tldr: A Franka Panda arm must put the seventh mahjong tile from the left, as seen from the robot, on a placemat. The tile is specified only by its position in the row of tiles, so the arm has to count along the row to work out which one is meant before picking it up.
steps: count to the 7th tile from the left as seen from the robot

why.perception: 7th tile from the left: ordinal spatial grounding
why.transport: tile onto the placemat [goal concerns where one object ends up: tile onto the placemat]

vlabench/select_poker_spatial.n: Pick up the fourth card from left
vlabench/select_poker_spatial.tldr: A Franka Panda arm must pick up the fourth playing card from the left, as seen from the robot, out of its holder and hold it up in the air. The card is specified only by its position in the row, so the arm has to count along the cards before grasping the thin card and lifting it clear.
steps: count to the 4th card from the left as seen from the robot
out of its holder and held up to z >= 0.9 m

why.perception: 4th card from the left: ordinal spatial grounding
why.transport: pick the card from its holder and lift it to z >= 0.9 m [goal concerns where one object ends up: pick the card from its holder and lift it to z >= 0.9 m]

humanoidbench/loco_balance_hard.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid starts standing on a balance board that rides on top of a rolling sphere and must stay on it, upright and still, for the whole episode. The footing is inherently unstable, so the humanoid needs constant fine balance corrections with gentle joint effort, and the episode is lost as soon as the board touches the ground or the humanoid sags too low.
steps: upright and still on the board over the rolling sphere for the whole episode

why.locomotion: stand on a balance board riding a rolling cylinder, upright and still, for the whole episode

humanoidbench/loco_hurdle.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid must run forward down a walled track past a line of hurdles without touching the side or back walls and without falling. The target pace is a sprint rather than a walk, and each hurdle is a solid barrier across the whole track that has to be cleared, so slow, quasi-static motion cannot succeed.
steps: sprint (~5 m/s) down the walled track without touching walls

why.locomotion: run forward down the walled track and over the hurdles without falling
why.dynamic: running at ~5 m/s and getting over 37.5 cm solid hurdles
why.dynamic.motion: the speed target is a sprint (~5 m/s) and each hurdle is a solid box to clear: a walk-speed or quasi-static path scores far below the bar

humanoidbench/loco_sit_simple.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid must lower itself onto a chair and stay seated, upright and still. The challenge is the transition: it has to bring its pelvis over the seat and settle to seated height quickly yet steadily, without toppling or ending up beside the chair, and then hold the seated posture with little effort.
steps: sit down on the chair with the pelvis over the seat
seated, upright and still until the episode ends

why.locomotion: sit the robot down on the chair and keep it seated, upright and still

humanoidbench/loco_walk.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid on flat ground must walk forward at a modest walking pace and keep walking without falling over. It is the basic locomotion test: the gait has to make steady forward progress, stay upright and use little actuator effort, because any fall ends the episode.
steps: forward at about 1 m/s without falling

why.locomotion: walk the H1 forward at ~1 m/s with its own joint control, without falling

humanoidbench/manip_bookshelf_simple.n: Shelve five objects in shade order
humanoidbench/manip_bookshelf_simple.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two five-finger Shadow hands must pick five red-tinted objects out of a set of twelve, the other seven being grey, and put each on its own place on a bookshelf, one at a time, from palest to darkest. Each destination is shown only as a translucent copy of the object, so the robot has to rank objects by shade and carry out five placements in the required order.
steps: the five red-tinted ones ranked from palest to darkest
its translucent target slot on the bookshelf, palest first

why.planning: five placements in a required order, palest first and darkest last
why.arrangement: put five objects onto their places on the bookshelf [five objects each to its own place, in shade order]

humanoidbench/manip_cube.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow hands has a cube starting just above each palm and must rotate both cubes to a goal orientation without dropping either one. The target is shown only as a translucent cube, and close is not good enough because only a precise orientation match counts, so both hands need careful in-hand finger work while the humanoid keeps standing still.
steps: goal orientation in each hand without dropping it

why.precision-contact: in-hand rotation of a cube in each Shadow hand to a goal orientation without dropping it
why.perception: the goal orientation is shown only as a translucent cube with the same faces in the image (no pose given in standard mode)

humanoidbench/manip_door.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid must walk up to a closed door, press its handle, pull the hinged door open towards itself and then walk through to the other side. It combines walking with a contact-heavy interaction with an articulated object: the door is heavy, so the humanoid has to open it while staying upright and then carry its torso through the doorway.
steps: through the doorway, torso past the door

why.articulated: press the door handle and pull the heavy hinged door open
why.locomotion: walk to the door and walk the torso through the doorway (a large reward term) with the H1's own leg control
why.navigation: travel from the start through the doorway to the other side

humanoidbench/manip_powerlift.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow hands must lift a very heavy dumbbell from the floor to well above its head and keep it there for most of the episode. This is a whole-body effort with no balance controller supplied: the humanoid has to grip the weight, drive it upward using its whole body, and stay standing while holding it aloft.
steps: about 2 m overhead from the floor
overhead for most of the episode while standing

why.locomotion: a whole-body lift from the floor to overhead with no balance controller
why.transport: lift the ~54 kg dumbbell from the floor to about 2 m and hold it there [one dumbbell lifted overhead and held]

humanoidbench/manip_room.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow hands must tidy a room by gathering six loose objects (a chair, a trophy, headphones, two packages and a snow globe) close together instead of spread out. No target positions are given and the objects start out of reach, so the humanoid has to walk around, find the right items among fixed furniture such as a table and bookshelf, and move them one by one.

why.perception: no object positions are given: the six named loose objects must be found and told apart from the fixed table and bookshelf in the cameras
why.arrangement: gather six loose objects (chair, trophy, headphones, two packages, snow globe) close together [six objects gathered close to one another]

humanoidbench/manip_window.n: Wipe a window with a tool
humanoidbench/manip_window.tldr: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow hands must catch a wiping tool that starts in mid-air in front of its hands and falls almost at once unless gripped, then use it to wipe a window with steady up-and-down strokes. The tool has to stay pressed against the glass, so the task needs a quick grasp followed by sustained contact while both hands keep hold.

steady up-and-down strokes with the tool kept in contact with the glass

why.precision-contact: wipe the window: most of the reward is paid only while the tool stays in contact with the glass
why.tool-use: grasp the wiping tool and use it on the window

molmospaces/close.n: Close a cabinet door in a house
molmospaces/close.tldr: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must shut a cabinet whose hinged door starts about half open. The door must end up nearly closed and stay that way, so the arm has to push a swinging door through its arc and not leave it drifting back open.

why.articulated: close a cabinet's hinged door from 50% open to at most 15%

molmospaces/open.n: Open a dishwasher in a house
molmospaces/open.tldr: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pull a dishwasher door away from its closed position by a clear amount. Any dishwasher in the room counts, so the arm first has to find one and then work out where to grip or hook the hinged door to swing it open.

why.articulated: open any cabinet joint in the room by at least 15%

molmospaces/pick.n: Pick up a pie in a house
molmospaces/pick.tldr: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pick up a pie and lift it a little clear of where it sat. At the end only the robot may be touching the pie, and since it is an irregular model from a large library of 3D assets, a suitable grasp has to be found from the scene.

why.transport: pick up the light switch plate and lift it 1 cm [one object: lift the light switch plate]

molmospaces/pick_and_place.n: Put a bottle into an ashtray
molmospaces/pick_and_place.tldr: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pick up a purple bottle with a white cap and set it in or on a clear ashtray with notches. why.perception: open-vocabulary Objaverse description ('realistic small white bird with feathers') grounded among >= 5 objects within 30 cm
why.transport: bird figurine into the black bowl [one object: the bird figurine into the bowl]

molmospaces/pick_and_place_color.n: Place an object in the right-colour bowl
molmospaces/pick_and_place_color.tldr: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pick up a small dark bird and put it in or on the red bowl. molmospaces/navigate_to.n: Find and approach a table lamp

within 1.5 m of the lamp with the lamp visible in the head camera

molmospaces/open_door.n: Pull a door open with RB-Y1
molmospaces/open_door.tldr: A Rainbow RB-Y1 wheeled mobile manipulator, with a torso, two arms and a head camera, must pull a door open in a simulated house until the door has swung most of the way open. why.articulated: pull a door open to at least 67% of its 90-degree range with the mobile RB-Y1

its assigned tall compartment (cuboid_i into cupboard_i)

why.perception: the target is the green square among red, blue and yellow decoy squares

kinder/scoop_pour_i01.tldr: A TidyBot++ wheeled mobile manipulator with an arm and gripper must move a large number of small dark-red cubes from a yellow bin into a green bin, with a scoop available in the scene. kinder/sweep_simple_i01.n: Sweep floor cubes into a box

why.precision-contact: non-prehensile sweeping of many cubes needs controlled, sustained wiper contact
why.tool-use: the cubes are swept with the wiper standing near them

dexjoco/pinch_tongs.n: Open and close kitchen tongs in the air
dexjoco/pinch_tongs.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm with a four-finger Allegro hand must pick up a pair of kitchen tongs from the table and, while holding them up in the air, open and close them several times by working their hinge. The same hand has to grip the tongs and squeeze them, so grasping and in-hand actuation must happen together.
steps: held at least 0.10 m above the table
open (0.1 rad) to closed (-0.07 rad) each pinch, while held up
at least 0.10 m up for 30 control steps after three pinches

why.articulated: open and close the tongs' hinge three times (>= 0.1 rad to <= -0.07 rad)
why.precision-contact: the tongs must be worked in hand while held at least 10 cm up: grasp and actuation by the same fingers

dexjoco/water_plant.n: Spray a potted plant with a spray bottle
dexjoco/water_plant.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm with a four-finger Allegro hand must pick up a spray bottle, hold its nozzle near a potted plant while pointing it at the plant, and pull the trigger and keep it pulled for a short while. The trigger is a small hinge worked by the index and middle fingers, and pulling it while the nozzle is away from the plant fails, so aim and finger force both matter.
steps: within 0.2 m of the plant with the spray aimed within 45 degrees
pulled past 0.34 rad, only while the nozzle is in the zone
kept pulled for 30 control steps (0.6 s)

why.tool-use: hold the spray bottle near the plant and aim its spray direction within 45 degrees of the plant
why.articulated: pull and hold the bottle's hinged trigger past 0.34 rad for 30 steps

myosuite/arm_reach.n: Reach a target with a muscle-driven arm
myosuite/arm_reach.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human shoulder, arm and hand, hanging at its side and driven only by commands to its muscles, must bring its index fingertip to a small target sphere in front of the body and hold it there. With no joint controller, many muscles must be coordinated to reach a precise point in space.
steps: target sphere in front of the body
within 1.25 cm of the target for 1 s

myosuite/baoding.n: Baoding balls in a muscle-driven hand
myosuite/baoding.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, holds two balls and must rotate them around each other so that each follows its own moving target marker as the targets circle the palm for a full orbit. The balls must not fall out, and the pair of moving targets demands continuous, finely coordinated finger muscle control.
steps: each ball follows its moving target through one full orbit in the palm

why.precision-contact: rotate two Baoding balls around each other in the palm, each within 1.5 cm of its moving target for a full orbit

myosuite/bimanual.n: Hand an object to a prosthetic hand
myosuite/bimanual.tldr: A musculoskeletal right arm and hand next to a motorized prosthetic left arm, standing at a table, must pick up an object with the biological hand, pass it to the prosthetic hand and set it on a goal pillar on the far side. It has to be held at each stage and must never touch the table or floor, so the exchange between two very different hands needs careful timing.
steps: from the biological hand to the prosthetic hand, never touching table or floor
goal pillar on the far side, touching only the pillar

why.transport: pick the object up with the MyoHand, hand it over to the prosthetic MPL hand and place it on the goal pillar [one object handed over and placed on the pillar]

myosuite/chase_tag.n: Chase and tag an opponent on foot
myosuite/chase_tag.tldr: A free-standing musculoskeletal model of a human torso and both legs, driven by many leg muscles, must walk across a square arena to bring its pelvis close to an opponent standing in it, within a time limit. It must stay upright and inside the arena, so walking with muscle-level control is the main challenge, and in this instance the opponent does not move.
steps: walk across the arena to within 0.5 m of the opponent, upright, inside the arena, within 20 s

why.locomotion: walk the 80-muscle MyoLegs to an opponent within 20 s without falling
why.navigation: the opponent stands somewhere in the 13 x 13 m arena; its position is not given and must be reached

myosuite/dex_airplane_fly.n: Fly a toy airplane along a recorded motion
myosuite/dex_airplane_fly.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must lift a toy airplane from a table and move it through the air so that its position and tilt follow a recorded human motion-capture reference. Matching a moving reference with an object in the grip demands a stable grasp and continuous finger control.
steps: flown through the air along the recorded 1.98 s motion, position and tilt tracked

why.transport: lift the toy airplane and fly it through the air along MyoDex's recorded 1.98 s motion (orientation counts) [one airplane moved along a reference motion]

myosuite/dex_apple_lift.n: Lift an apple along a recorded motion
myosuite/dex_apple_lift.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose beside an apple on a table must lift the apple so that its path follows a recorded human motion-capture reference. The grasp has to hold a round object while it tracks a moving reference, using only muscle-level commands to the hand.
steps: raised along the recorded 1.14 s lift motion

why.transport: lift the apple along MyoDex's recorded 1.14 s lift motion [one apple lifted along a reference motion]

myosuite/dex_bunny_inspect.n: Lift and turn a bunny to inspect it
myosuite/dex_bunny_inspect.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must lift a Stanford bunny figure from a table and turn it as if looking it over, so that its position and rotation follow a recorded human motion-capture reference. Orientation counts, so the grip must hold an irregular shape while it is rotated.
steps: raised from the table along the recorded motion
turned over to look at it, rotation tracked along the recorded 1.98 s motion

why.transport: lift the Stanford bunny and turn it along MyoDex's recorded 1.98 s inspect motion (orientation counts) [one bunny lifted and turned along a reference motion]

myosuite/dex_cup_pour.n: Lift and tilt a cup as if pouring
myosuite/dex_cup_pour.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must lift a cup from a table and tilt it as if pouring, so that the cup's position and rotation follow a recorded human motion-capture reference. The grasp has to stay secure through the tilt while only muscle-level commands drive the hand.
steps: raised from the table along the recorded motion
tilted as if pouring, rotation tracked along the recorded 1.62 s motion

why.transport: lift the cup and tilt it as if pouring, along MyoDex's recorded 1.62 s motion [one cup lifted and tilted along a reference motion]

myosuite/dex_cylinder_pass.n: Present a cylinder for a hand-over
myosuite/dex_cylinder_pass.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must pick up a small cylinder from a table and present it as if offering it for a hand-over, so that the cylinder's path follows a recorded human motion-capture reference. The hand must keep a firm grip while tracking the reference.
steps: picked up and presented for a hand-over along the recorded 1.72 s motion

why.transport: pick up the small cylinder and present it for a hand-over along MyoDex's recorded 1.72 s motion [one cylinder lifted and presented along a reference motion]

myosuite/dex_hammer_use.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must grasp a hammer lying on a table and swing it, so that its position and rotation follow a recorded human motion-capture reference. The heavy tool must be held firmly through a fast swing, and orientation counts as well as position.
steps: grasped and swung along the recorded 1.98 s motion, rotation tracked

why.transport: grasp the hammer and move it along MyoDex's recorded 1.98 s swing (orientation counts) [one hammer moved along a reference swing]

myosuite/die_reorient.n: Reorient a die in a muscle-driven hand
myosuite/die_reorient.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, holds a die and must rotate it in the hand until it matches the pose shown by a translucent target die, then keep it there for a moment. The die must not be dropped, and every turn has to be achieved with finger muscles alone.
steps: rotated in the hand to the target pose (2.5 cm, 0.262 rad)
at the target pose for 1 s

why.precision-contact: in-hand reorientation of a die to a target pose (2.5 cm, 0.262 rad) held 1 s

myosuite/hand_pose.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, starting in a rest posture, must curl its fingers, thumb and wrist into a given target pose, shown by translucent fingertip markers, and hold it for a moment. All of the joint angles have to be matched together through muscle commands rather than joint control.
steps: target pose of 23 joint angles (error norm below 0.7 rad)

myosuite/hand_reach.n: Put all five fingertips on targets
myosuite/hand_reach.tldr: A relaxed musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand must move the thumb and all four fingertips onto five small target spheres at once and hold them there for a moment. Five goals have to be reached together through muscle-level control, so the fingers must be coordinated to reach precise points in space.
steps: onto its target sphere, all five at once
on the five targets for 1 s

myosuite/key_turn.n: Turn a key with a thumb-index pinch
myosuite/key_turn.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand has a key in a lock in front of the palm, with its head between thumb and index finger, and must turn the key by more than half a turn and hold it there. The turn needs a sustained pinch with fingertips that stay on the key head, driven only by muscle commands.
steps: more than half a turn (3.14 rad) with a thumb-index pinch
turned past half a turn for 1 s

why.articulated: turn the key on its hinge by more than half a turn and hold it
why.precision-contact: the key is turned by a sustained thumb-index pinch; fingertips more than 10 cm from the key head end the episode

myosuite/obj_hold.n: Hold an object in the palm
myosuite/obj_hold.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, has a small object resting in the palm and must keep the object at a goal point just above it for a moment. The object falls if the fingers do not grip it, so the hand has to close around it and hold it steady using muscle commands alone.
steps: gripped and held at the goal point just above the palm
within 1 cm of the goal for 1 s

why.transport: grip the object resting in the hand and hold its centre within 1 cm of the goal for 1 s [one object held at the goal]

myosuite/obj_reorient.n: Reorient an object held in the hand
myosuite/obj_reorient.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, has an object resting on its fingers and must turn it in the hand until its orientation matches a translucent target copy, then keep it there for a moment. The object is one of several possible shapes, and it must not be dropped while the fingers reposition it.
steps: reoriented in the hand to the target orientation (cosine above 0.95)
at the target orientation for 1 s

why.precision-contact: in-hand reorientation of the held object to the target orientation (cosine > 0.95), held 1 s

myosuite/osl_run.n: Run a track with a prosthetic leg
myosuite/osl_run.tldr: A free-standing musculoskeletal human model whose right leg is a motorised knee-and-ankle prosthesis must run forward along a straight flat track to the finish line, staying on its feet and near the centre line. Only the leg muscles are commanded, while the prosthesis runs its own controller, so a stable running gait has to be produced with a mixed biological and robotic body.
steps: run 29 m along the track to the finish, within 1 m of the centre line, on its feet

why.locomotion: move 29 m down the track on a musculoskeletal leg plus a powered knee-ankle prosthesis, without falling

myosuite/pen_twirl.n: Twirl a pen to a target direction
myosuite/pen_twirl.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, has a pen lying across its fingers and must rotate the pen in the hand until it points along the direction shown by a translucent target pen, then keep it there for a moment. The pen must not be dropped, and spinning a long thin object takes careful finger muscle coordination.
steps: rotated in the hand until its axis matches the target orientation
at the target orientation for 1 s

why.precision-contact: in-hand rotation of the pen until its axis matches the target orientation, held 1 s

myosuite/relocate.n: Place an object in a receptacle by hand
myosuite/relocate.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human shoulder, arm and hand in front of a table must pick up an object standing on it and put it in a target receptacle, keeping it there for a moment. The whole arm and hand are driven by muscle commands, so reaching, grasping and carrying must all be coordinated without a joint controller.

why.transport: pick the object up from the table and put it in the target receptacle [one object into the receptacle]

myosuite/sarc_key_turn.n: Turn a key with weakened muscles
myosuite/sarc_key_turn.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand with muscles weakened to mimic age-related muscle loss has a key in a lock in front of the palm, and must turn the key by more than half a turn and hold it there. With every muscle at reduced strength, the sustained thumb-index pinch needed to turn the key is much harder to produce.
steps: more than half a turn (3.14 rad) with every muscle at half force
turned past half a turn for 1 s

why.articulated: turn the key on its hinge by more than half a turn and hold it
why.precision-contact: the turn needs a sustained thumb-index pinch, with every muscle at half force

myosuite/soccer.n: Score a goal past a goalkeeper
myosuite/soccer.tldr: A free-standing musculoskeletal human model, with a very large number of leg muscles, stands on a soccer pitch with a ball in front of it and must kick the ball into the goal past a goalkeeper within a time limit. The kick must be hard enough to carry the ball to the goal while the body stays upright, which makes balance and striking power the main challenges.
steps: kicked into the goal past the goalkeeper within 10 s

why.locomotion: the 290-muscle MyoLegs must stay on its feet and kick with a leg
why.dynamic: the ball must be kicked into the goal
why.dynamic.motion: a kick: the ball has to be struck to travel into the goal past the goalkeeper within 10 s; a quasi-static push of the ball would not get it there

myosuite/table_tennis.tldr: A musculoskeletal model of a human torso, right arm and hand, on a pelvis that slides on the floor, holds a paddle at a table-tennis table and must return a served ball so that it lands on the opponent's half. The ball arrives quickly from the far side, so the model must watch its flight and hit it cleanly, using only muscle-level commands.
steps: returned so it lands on the opponent's half after one paddle touch

why.tool-use: return the ball with the paddle held in the right hand
why.dynamic: scene: the ball is served at reset; motion: the return is a timed strike
why.dynamic.motion: the served ball must be struck so that it carries onto the opponent's half: a slow paddle cannot return it
why.feedback: the served ball's flight must be observed to intercept it within the 3 s rally

roboarc/blanket_flatten_01.n: Spread a blanket flat on a table
roboarc/blanket_flatten_01.tldr: Two ALOHA arms at a table must unfold a cloth blanket and spread it flat on the tabletop without overlaps or excessive stretching, then let go and withdraw. The soft sheet moves unpredictably when grasped, so the arms must flatten nearly all of it, keep it down on the table and leave it still. This is a very easy variation.
steps: unfolded and spread flat on the table, at least 95 percent coverage

why.deformable-fluid: unfold and spread a simulated cloth blanket (MuJoCo PBD flex / VBD cloth) to >=95% top-view coverage, no overlaps, edges stretched <=1.15x

roboarc/blanket_fold_01.n: Fold a blanket to match a target
roboarc/blanket_fold_01.tldr: Two ALOHA arms at a table must fold a blanket that starts lying flat in half, turning the far half over onto the near half so the stack matches target images, then let go and withdraw. The soft cloth must be creased cleanly, with its corners landing in the right places and the far half ending upside down on top.
steps: far half turned over onto the near half, two layers 600 x 240 mm

why.deformable-fluid: fold a simulated cloth blanket into a target fold graded on corner positions, layer order and outline IoU

roboarc/blanket_fold_02.n: Fold a blanket to match a target
roboarc/blanket_fold_02.tldr: Two ALOHA arms at a table must fold a flat blanket in half, then dog-ear the top layer by turning one of its corners over onto it, so the result matches target images, and then let go and withdraw. The two ordered folds must give the right layer order and corner positions in a soft cloth that deforms unpredictably.
steps: far half turned over onto the near half, two layers 600 x 240 mm
dog-ear: near-left corner of the top layer turned over onto the top layer alone

why.deformable-fluid: fold a simulated cloth blanket into a target fold graded on corner positions, layer order and outline IoU

roboarc/blanket_fold_03.n: Fold a blanket to match a target
roboarc/blanket_fold_03.tldr: Two ALOHA arms at a table must fold a blanket in half, turning the far half over onto the near half to match target images, then let go and withdraw. Here the blanket starts folded over on itself, so the arms must handle that existing layering and still end with the right layer order and corner positions.
steps: unfolded flat from its folded-over start
far half turned over onto the near half, two layers 600 x 240 mm

why.deformable-fluid: fold a simulated cloth blanket into a target fold graded on corner positions, layer order and outline IoU

roboarc/blanket_fold_04.n: Fold a blanket to match a target
roboarc/blanket_fold_04.tldr: Two ALOHA arms at a table must refold a blanket that starts folded over on itself: first in half, then with a dog-ear on the top layer made by turning one corner over, to match target images before letting go and withdrawing. The folds must be done in that order because layer order is checked, on a soft cloth that deforms unpredictably.
steps: unfolded flat from its folded-over start
far half turned over onto the near half, two layers 600 x 240 mm
dog-ear: near-left corner of the top layer turned over onto the top layer alone

roboarc/blanket_fold_05.n: Fold a blanket to match a target
roboarc/blanket_fold_05.tldr: Two ALOHA arms at a table must refold a blanket that starts folded over on itself, first in half and then with a dog-ear on the top layer, to match target images before letting go and withdrawing. A fixed block stands beyond the far side of the blanket, and the cloth must finish on the table, not on the block.
steps: unfolded flat from its folded-over start
far half turned over onto the near half, two layers 600 x 240 mm
dog-ear on the table, cloth ending on the table and not on the fixed block

roboarc/buzz_wire_3d_01.n: Trace a 3D wire without touching it
roboarc/buzz_wire_3d_01.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm must guide the metal loop of a wooden-handled wand along a whole bent 3D wire from start to finish without any metal touching the wire, then set the wand down on a finish support and let go. The clearance is tiny, so the loop must stay centred along the route. This is the very easy variation.
steps: whole 3D wire from start to finish with no metal touching it
finish support within 5 mm and 10 degrees of the target pose

why.transport: the wand must end resting on the finish support within 5 mm and 10 deg of the target pose [only the wand's final resting pose on the finish support is placed]

The piece only escapes through a non-obvious sequence of rotations and slides with tight clearances. This is the window-change variant of the cage.

every spike inside the green dashed goal square, cage parts left on the puzzle side

why.planning: Hanayama-style disentanglement puzzle: the separating path is a non-obvious sequence of rotations and slides
why.transport: the spiked ball/star/owl must be placed entirely inside the green goal square, the rest kept behind a separator [only the freed ball/star/owl is placed in the goal square; the cage stays]

roboarc/ikea_eket.n: Build an EKET cabinet frame from panels
roboarc/ikea_eket.tldr: On a table, two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands must assemble an IKEA EKET cabinet frame: slide both side panels into the top panel, fit the back panel into its grooves, slide the bottom panel onto the sides, and leave the cabinet standing by itself. The panels join through mitres, keyholes and dowels with almost no slack, every joint has to be made in a fixed order, and grasps hold only by finger friction.
steps: entered and slid into the top panel through mitre and keyholes, frame joint latched (0.25-0.8 mm, 0.1-1 deg)
slid into its grooves in the top and side panels
entered and slid onto both side panels, both joints latched, cabinet left standing on the table

why.precision-contact: slide side, back and bottom panels into the top panel through mitres, keyholes, dowels and grooves; each slide must reach its goal within 0.25-0.8 mm and 0.1-1 deg with panel contact
why.planning: seven operations in a fixed dependent order (side A entry/slide, side B entry/slide, back slide, bottom entry/slide), each gated against the top panel

roboarc/ikea_gladom.n: Assemble a GLADOM tray table with screws
roboarc/ikea_gladom.tldr: Working with two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands, the robot must build an IKEA GLADOM tray table: cross one leg frame into the other, drive the long and bottom screws, add the ring and fasten it with two more screws, then rest the loose tray on the ring. The small screws advance only when turned, using the hex driver that stands in the scene, and each step needs the previous parts seated and aligned.
steps: crossed into frame A, retention latched (0.8 mm gap, 1 mm lateral, 2 deg)
driven into frame A's nut sleeves with the hex driver, seated and latched
at its assembled pose on the frames
driven with the hex driver into two distinct ring receivers, seated and latched
free on the ring, supported by it (within 7.5 deg)

why.precision-contact: cross frame B into frame A and drive four screws into SDF nut sleeves (0.5 mm pitch, turned only), every part within 0.8 mm gap / 1 mm lateral / 2 deg of its assembled pose
why.tool-use: the screws have hex sockets and are driven with the free hex driver that stands in the scene (scene layout hex_driver; seated heads cannot be gripped)
why.planning: dependent chain: cross frame B, drive long and bottom screws (need frame B aligned), place the ring, drive its two screws (need the ring placed), set the tray on the ring

roboarc/ikea_ikea365.n: Rebuild a serving stand and set its bowl
roboarc/ikea_ikea365.tldr: Here two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands must rebuild an IKEA 365+ serving stand: unscrew the screw from one member and set it aside, lay the second member across the first, drive the screw back in through both, turn the stand over and place the bowl on it. The steps must happen in this order, the small screw is driven with a screwdriver from the scene, and the finished stand must rest firmly with its bowl.
steps: parked aside, clear of the members
laid across member A, holes in line
returned into the hole through both members
driven through both members until seated (axial 0.1 mm, lateral 0.6 mm, axis 1.5 deg)
turned over, member A's z axis pointing down
on the stand, touching the members, bench carrying the load

why.precision-contact: unthread and reinstall an M4 x 0.5 screw through both members (turned only) until seated: axial 0.1 mm, lateral 0.6 mm, axis 1.5 deg
why.tool-use: the screw is driven with the screwdriver lying in the scene (benchmark doc: 'a screw driven with a screwdriver'; the reference spins it on the screw head)
why.planning: seven operations accepted in order: remove screw, park it, cross the members, return screw, reinstall it, turn the stand over, place the bowl

roboarc/ikea_lack.n: Screw four legs onto a LACK table
roboarc/ikea_lack.tldr: Using two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands, the robot must screw all four legs of an IKEA LACK side table onto the threaded studs of its tabletop, which lies studs up, one leg per stud, and let go with every leg seated. Each leg moves down only while it is being turned through several full revolutions, so the hands must grip it by friction alone, keep it on the thread and repeat this four times.
steps: screwed onto a distinct threaded stud, about six turns until seated and latched (0-12 mm, 20 mm, 10 deg)

why.precision-contact: screw four legs onto the tabletop's M16 threaded studs; a leg advances only by being turned (about six turns) until seated and latched

roboarc/ikea_stegesund.n: Build a STEGESUND roll stand with a hex key
roboarc/ikea_stegesund.tldr: With two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands, the robot must build an IKEA STEGESUND roll stand: press the two leg halves together at their crossings, push the shelf in, drive four bolts into the shelf with a hex key, stand the frame upright and drop the top rod into its notches. The bolts turn only through the key seated in their sockets, and every part must end closely aligned with the frame.
steps: pressed onto half A at the two leg crossings (0.6 mm, 1 deg)
pushed in from the foot end to its assembled pose (0.6 mm, 1 deg)
driven through the legs into the shelf's rail ends with the hex key, seated and welded
stood upright, half A's z axis within 1 deg of vertical
dropped into the two crotches (3 mm, 1 deg)

why.precision-contact: press-fit half B onto half A, push the shelf in and thread four bolts until seated: parts within 0.6 mm and 1 deg of their assembled poses
why.tool-use: drive the four bolts through the legs into the shelf's rail ends with the hex key in their 4 mm sockets
why.planning: dependent sequence: press the halves together, push the shelf in, drive four bolts with the hex key, stand the frame up, drop the top rod into the crotches

roboarc/ikea_svallet.n: Fit a lamp shade and screw in the bulb
roboarc/ikea_svallet.tldr: Two ViperX arms of an ALOHA 2 robot must finish an IKEA SVALLET work lamp: push the shade's key down into the socket on top of the stand until a spring jaw snaps over it, then screw the bulb upward into the shade's socket until it seats. The snap needs a firm, well-aligned press, the bulb advances only by being turned, and the lamp must stay upright on the bench afterwards.
steps: pressed down into the stand-column socket until the spring jaw snaps over it, stand kept within 3 deg of upright
turned up into the shade's socket until it seats

why.precision-contact: press the shade's key into the stand socket until a spring jaw snaps over its barb, then screw the E12 bulb (turned only) into the shade's socket until it seats within the connector gates

roboarc/ikea_variera.n: Assemble a VARIERA shelf insert with screws
roboarc/ikea_variera.tldr: At a bench, two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands must assemble an IKEA VARIERA shelf insert: set the two side frames in place, lower the shelf onto them and drive four small screws through the shelf into the frames until their heads seat. The screws advance only when turned with the screwdriver provided in the scene, and nothing but the threads holds the parts together, so the frames must stay aligned throughout.
steps: on the bench at its assembled place
lowered onto both side frames, holes over the receivers
driven with the screwdriver through the shelf holes into four distinct receivers, heads seated (0.2 mm, 0.6 mm, 1.5 deg)

why.precision-contact: drive four screws (0.5 mm pitch SDF threads, turned only) through the shelf holes into the frame receivers, heads seated within 0.2 mm axial / 0.6 mm lateral / 1.5 deg
why.tool-use: the screws are driven with the screwdriver in its stand in the scene (benchmark doc: 'screws driven with a screwdriver'; the reference demo ends holding it)
why.planning: dependent order: place both side frames, lower the shelf onto them, then drive the four screws (seven operations, no welds hold the parts meanwhile)

roboarc/ikea_vesken.n: Snap together a VESKEN shelf unit
roboarc/ikea_vesken.tldr: The task gives two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands the parts of an IKEA VESKEN shelf unit to build: snap four feet into the bottom tray, then columns and trays level by level up to the top, and finally four caps into the top tray. All twenty-three snap connections must be made in that order, each pin pressed past a spring jaw and seated precisely, which makes this a very long, contact-heavy build.
steps: snapped into the bottom tray from below
snapped into the top tray, all 23 snaps within gates, feet on the bench

why.precision-contact: 23 snap connections: hooked pins pressed past spring jaws and seated within 0.6 mm axial, 0.8 mm lateral, 2 deg
why.planning: all 23 snaps must be made in the source order, each depending on the previous (feet, columns, tray, columns, tray, columns, tray, caps)

roboarc/lock_picking_01.n: Thread a key through rotor plates
roboarc/lock_picking_01.tldr: A single Franka arm with a two-finger parallel gripper must pick up a two-tab key from its rest and push it through a stack of two jointed rotor plates and a final end plate, respecting their slots and stops. The key's leading tab is longer than the second, the clearances are tiny, and the tabs must line up with each plate's slot, so the key needs an ordered insert-and-rotate sequence.
steps: through two rotor plates and the END plate
tabs lined up with each rotor slot, within stop limits

why.precision-contact: insert a key shaft through 3-5 bores with ~1 mm radial and <0.5 deg tilt tolerance (key-in-lock)
why.articulated: the rotor plates are jointed with travel stops; their slots must be aligned by the key tabs and exceeding a stop fails
why.planning: lock puzzle: tab/slot alignment through successive rotors needs an ordered insert-and-rotate sequence

roboarc/orbits_01.n: Free a cord loop from an orbit puzzle
roboarc/orbits_01.tldr: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must free a cord loop with a wooden handle from a fixed post and stopper ball and place the whole cord and handle inside a green dashed goal square, leaving the post, ball and base on the puzzle side. The cord is floppy and the loop has to be passed around the post and ball in a non-obvious order. This instance is the very easy variant.
steps: free of the post and stopper ball

why.deformable-fluid: the cord is a 53-link spring-jointed chain that must be manipulated off the post and stopper ball
why.planning: Orbits disentanglement puzzle: the loop must pass around post and ball in a non-obvious order

The rope is floppy, the openings are identified only by colour, and the order and direction of each pass matter without adding extra crossings.
steps: through cyan ring, then green ring in order and direction

why.deformable-fluid: thread a simulated rope (200-link capsule chain) through rings/grommets without extra crossings
why.perception: rings and wall grommets are identified only by colour names (cyan, green, purple, ...) and must be threaded in that order and direction

robodojo/align_blocks.n: Align three blocks with a set square
robodojo/align_blocks.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, standing at a table, must use a triangular set square as a pushing tool to shove three cubes into one straight, neatly squared row without ever lifting a cube, then return to the home pose. Success depends on controlled sweeping contact with a held tool, because the cubes must end up on one line and turned the same way.
steps: one straight row, each cube turned along the row, none lifted

why.tool-use: hold the set square and use it to push three cubes into a row, without lifting any cube
why.precision-contact: cube centres within 8 mm of one line and each cube yawed within 8 degrees of the row, by pushing only

robodojo/arrange_largest_number.n: Arrange digit blocks into largest number
robodojo/arrange_largest_number.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must read the digits printed on four or five number blocks and place them one per mat along a row so that the digits, read in order, spell the largest possible number. The challenge is reading the digits from camera images and ranking them from largest to smallest before moving anything, then placing each block upright on its own mat.
steps: read the digits and rank them largest to smallest
one per mat, largest digit on the first mat, upright

why.perception: the digits printed on the blocks must be read from the images
why.planning: ranking: the blocks must be ordered so they form the largest possible number
why.arrangement: place 4-5 digit blocks upright on a row of mats [4-5 digit blocks ranked onto a row of mats]

robodojo/arrange_largest_number_random.n: Order digit blocks to largest number, cluttered
robodojo/arrange_largest_number_random.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must read the digits printed on four or five number blocks and place them one per mat along a row so that the digits spell the largest possible number. This randomised variant uses different object models and adds clutter around the blocks, so spotting and reading the right digits is harder before any ranking and placing begins.
steps: read the digits among clutter and rank them largest to smallest
one per mat, largest digit on the first mat, upright

why.perception: the digits printed on the blocks must be read from the images (other models, clutter)
why.planning: ranking: the blocks must be ordered so they form the largest possible number
why.arrangement: place 4-5 digit blocks upright on a row of mats [4-5 digit blocks ranked onto a row of mats]

robodojo/build_tower.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, working at a table, must build a three-level tower from wooden blocks and boards: two pillars bridged by a long board, two more blocks and a second board above, then the top pieces. Each layer depends on the one below, so the order is fixed, and every piece must be placed accurately enough to stay stable and upright.
steps: on the table, left and right of the base board
on top of the two blocks

why.planning: dependent construction order: pillars, then board, then two blocks on the board, second board, then top pieces
why.arrangement: stack eight wooden blocks and boards into a three-level tower, every piece upright within 5 degrees [eight pieces built into a three-level tower]

robodojo/classify_objects.n: Sort small objects into three baskets
robodojo/classify_objects.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must sort the small objects on a table by category into three baskets, so that every item of one category lands in the same basket and each category gets its own. The categories are never named, so the robot has to work out from appearance which objects belong together, then carry out a long run of pick-and-place moves.
steps: work out the three categories by appearance
baskets, one whole category per basket

why.perception: the agent must work out the three categories and which objects belong together from appearance alone
why.arrangement: sort all small objects into three baskets [all objects sorted into three baskets by category]

robodojo/classify_objects_by_language.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must follow a written instruction that names which kind of object goes into the left, middle and right basket, here cars, watches and wooden toys, and sort every object accordingly. It tests grounding category words in what the objects look like and then placing many items without mixing up the baskets.
steps: match them to the named categories car, watch, wooden toy
left, middle, right basket as named

why.perception: objects must be assigned to categories named in the instruction (car, watch, wooden_toy) from their appearance
why.arrangement: put every object of three categories into its basket [all objects sorted into three baskets by category]

robodojo/cover_blocks.n: Cover blocks with cups, then uncover in order
robodojo/cover_blocks.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must place three cups over three coloured blocks one after another from left to right, remembering which colour ended up under which cup, then lift the cups off one at a time in the order red, green, blue. The blocks are hidden once covered, so success needs memory plus a long, ordered sequence of cup moves.
steps: note which colour is at the left, middle, right
over the three cubes, left to right, cups kept inverted
off the cubes in the order red, green, blue

why.perception: which colour (red, green, blue) sits under which cup must be read from the images before covering
why.planning: 6 ordered stages: cover left, middle, right, then uncover in colour order red, green, blue
why.arrangement: cover three cubes with inverted cups and uncover them again without displacing the cubes more than 5 cm [three cups placed over three blocks in order]

robodojo/deposit_coin.n: Drop a coin into a piggy bank
robodojo/deposit_coin.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must lift a coin out of a vertical coin holder and drop it through the slot of a piggy bank, then return to the home pose. The coin is thin and stands in its holder, and the slot is narrow, so both the grasp and the alignment above the slot demand care.

why.precision-contact: insert the coin through the piggy bank's slot so it drops inside

robodojo/fasten_screws.n: Seat nuts on matching coloured bolts
robodojo/fasten_screws.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must pick up three nuts and fit each one onto the bolt of the same colour, leaving every nut upright and centred before the grippers let go. Matching nuts to bolts is done by colour and the fit is tight, so alignment has to be nearly exact for a nut to seat properly.
steps: match each nut to the bolt of the same colour
onto the bolt of the same colour, upright and centred

why.precision-contact: seat three nuts on their bolts within 1 mm horizontally and 9 mm deep, upright
why.perception: each nut must go on the bolt of the same colour

robodojo/fill_egg_holder.n: Move four eggs into a lidded holder
robodojo/fill_egg_holder.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must move four eggs one by one from a basket into the cups of an egg holder and then swing the holder's hinged lid shut. The eggs are rounded and easy to knock about, and the run ends with a hinge motion, so many pick-and-place moves must lead cleanly into the final closing.

why.articulated: close the egg holder's hinged lid
why.arrangement: move four eggs from the basket into the holder's cups [four eggs into the holder's cups]

robodojo/fill_pen_holder.n: Drop pens into a held pen holder
robodojo/fill_pen_holder.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must use one arm to steady a pen holder while the other arm drops four pens into it tip down, then set the holder back upright on the table. The two arms have different jobs at the same time, and the pens must go in the right way up without toppling the holder.
steps: held steady by one arm while the pens go in

why.arrangement: drop four pens tip-down into a pen holder steadied by the other arm, then leave the holder upright [four pens into the holder]

robodojo/fold_clothes.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must fold a long-sleeved shirt lying flat on a table: first fold both sleeves in across the chest, then bring the bottom hem up to the shoulders, finishing with both arms back home and the grippers open. The cloth is simulated and deformable, the order of folds matters, and the robot works from camera images alone.
steps: folded up to the shoulders, after the sleeves

why.deformable-fluid: fold a simulated long-sleeve shirt (GPU PhysX cloth): sleeves across the chest, then hem to shoulders
why.planning: ordered folds: folding the hem before both sleeves are in fails the episode

robodojo/fold_clothes_random.n: Fold a shirt in a cluttered scene
robodojo/fold_clothes_random.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must fold a long-sleeved shirt lying flat on a table, first folding both sleeves in across the chest and then the bottom hem up to the shoulders. This randomised variant uses different object models and adds clutter, so the deformable cloth has to be handled with ordered folds while working only from camera images.
steps: folded up to the shoulders, after the sleeves

why.deformable-fluid: fold a simulated long-sleeve shirt (GPU PhysX cloth): sleeves across the chest, then hem to shoulders
why.planning: ordered folds: folding the hem before both sleeves are in fails the episode

robodojo/general_pickup.n: Lift a named object from clutter
robodojo/general_pickup.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must pick up one object that is named only by a short description, for instance a mint green pair of scissors, from among a crowd of other items and lift it clear of the surface. The target comes from a wide pool of everyday object types, so the robot must recognise it by appearance and grasp very different shapes.
steps: identify the one named by the description among the clutter

why.perception: the target is named only by a natural-language description (e.g. 'mint green scissors') among 10 clutter objects
why.transport: pick up the named object and lift it 10 cm [lift the one named object among clutter]

robodojo/hang_mugs.n: Hang three mugs on a rack
robodojo/hang_mugs.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must hang three mugs by their handles on the hooks of a mug rack, then return both arms home. The mugs start at varied angles, so the handle has to be located and hooked precisely onto the rack, which makes hanging an awkwardly oriented object the heart of the task.
steps: by the handle on the hooks of the mug rack

why.arrangement: hang all three mugs by their handles on the mug rack [three mugs hung on the rack]

robodojo/hang_mugs_random.n: Hang mugs on a rack amid clutter
robodojo/hang_mugs_random.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must hang three mugs by their handles on the hooks of a mug rack, then return home. This randomised variant uses different mug models and scatters many distractor objects over the table, so the robot must find each handle among clutter and still hook it precisely onto the rack.
steps: by the handle on the hooks of the mug rack, handles found among clutter

why.arrangement: hang all three mugs by their handles on the mug rack [three mugs hung on the rack]

robodojo/imitate_sorting_sequence.tldr: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers watches a second, demonstrator arm put five objects into the far basket one after another, then must place its own matching copies into its basket in the same order. The order exists only in the live demonstration, so the robot has to remember it, match each item to its twin and keep its own arms out of the way while the other arm works.
steps: watch the order in which it puts five objects into its basket
own basket, in the demonstrated order

why.dynamic: a support (opponent) arm demonstrates by placing five objects into the far basket during the episode
why.perception: each demonstrated object must be matched to its same-model copy on the agent's side
why.planning: five ordered placements; releasing an object before an earlier-demonstrated one is in fails at once
why.feedback: the required order exists only in the support arm's live demonstration; nothing in the text states it
