why.planning: 4 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: left, right, left, right strikes through three different gaps, then the goal
why.feedback: each return of the sliding puck must be observed to place and time the next strike

pandadyn/d04_shared_tray_transport_disch.n: Carry a tray with a loose ball together
pandadyn/d04_shared_tray_transport_disch.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms, each with a small fork cradling one end of a tray that holds a loose ball, must carry the tray together through two waypoints that form a turn, calm the ball after the environment pushes it, and then tip it out into a fixed basin. The ball may not leave the tray early and the tray may not drop, so both arms must move in careful step.
steps: level and steady with both forks supporting it
through two waypoints that make a turn, ball kept inside
back to rest near the tray centre after the environment push
exit position beside the fixed basin
fixed basin, tipped out of the tray

why.precision-contact: the loose ball must be kept on the jointly held tray and brought back to rest near the centre (balancing an object on another)
why.dynamic: the environment pushes the ball with an impulse mid-task (disturbance_recovery)
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: support, turn through two waypoints, recover from the push, align at exit, discharge
why.feedback: a mid-task perturbation (the push on the ball) must be observed and corrected
why.transport: two arms carry a shared tray with a loose ball through waypoints and tip the ball into a basin [the goal is one ball in the basin; the tray is the carrier]

pandadyn/d05_moving_ramp_relay.n: Relay a ball through a held channel
pandadyn/d05_moving_ramp_relay.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms face off: the left holds a cup with a ball in it and the right holds a straight, open-ended channel. The left arm passes the ball into the channel and catches it in flight as it leaves the far end, then repeats the relay with the channel held at a clearly different angle and finally delivers the ball into a fixed basin.
steps: inlet of the channel held by the right arm
at the channel outlet in free flight by the left cup
channel inlet again, channel at a clearly different orientation
at the channel outlet in free flight by the left cup

why.planning: 6 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: channel entry, exit, catch, a second relay at a channel orientation at least 0.30 rad different, catch and deliver
why.transport: pour the ball from the left cup into a channel held by the right arm, catch it at the outlet, repeat, then deliver it into a basin [one ball relayed and delivered into the basin]

pandadyn/d06_moving_bank_relay.n: Bank a puck off a rebound board
pandadyn/d06_moving_bank_relay.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms with paddles play a bank-shot game: the right paddle hits a low-friction puck that is already sliding in through a gap in a row of posts, and the left paddle acts as a rebound board that sends it back through the same gap. After a second strike and a rebound through the other gap with the board repositioned, the puck must cross a goal line untouched by the right paddle.
steps: right paddle: back through gap 0 to rebound off the left board
clearly different position and angle for the second rebound
right paddle: through gap 1, rebound off the moved board, across the goal line untouched

why.dynamic: a low-friction puck is already sliding toward the right paddle at t = 0
why.dynamic.motion: the right paddle must strike the puck twice so it travels back through specific gaps and finally across the goal line
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: strike, rebound through gap 0, strike, rebound through gap 1 with the left board moved, goal
why.feedback: the puck's rebounds must be observed to place the board and time the strikes

pandadyn/d07_spring_gate_switchyard.n: Swing a gate while shooting a puck
pandadyn/d07_spring_gate_switchyard.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms work around a low-friction puck in a U-shaped pen of bouncy rails: the left arm grips a spring-loaded swinging gate with its bare gripper while the right paddle drives the puck into the pen. The gate must be swung the opposite way at the moment the puck hits a side rail, after which the puck is intercepted and shot across a goal line with the gate still deflected.
steps: swung open one way by the left gripper holding it
right paddle: deep into the pen
swung to the opposite angle when the puck hits the upper rail, still gripped
across the goal line with the gate still deflected and the paddle not touching

why.articulated: the left gripper grips a spring-loaded swinging gate and swings it one way, then the other
why.dynamic: a puck slides inside a pen of bouncy rails
why.dynamic.motion: the right paddle hits the puck so that it travels deep into the pen, then intercepts it and shoots it across a goal line
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: open gate, loop shot, reconfigure the gate in time, intercept, final shot with the gate deflected
why.feedback: the gate must be at the opposite angle at the moment the running puck hits the upper rail: the puck must be watched

pandadyn/d08_pendulum_energy_relay.n: Swing and settle a pendulum together
pandadyn/d08_pendulum_energy_relay.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms, each holding a flat paddle, stand either side of a passive pendulum, a rod with a ball-shaped bob. The left paddle must push it into a swing, the right paddle must meet and brake it and then drive it back, and the left paddle touches it once more, after which the pendulum must hang almost straight down and nearly still.
steps: left paddle: swung out towards the right arm
right paddle meets and brakes the swing
right paddle: driven back out towards the left arm and released
left paddle touches it again and damps the swing
hanging almost straight down and almost still for one second

why.articulated: a passive hinged pendulum whose hinge angle and rate are the goal (excite, brake, return, hold still within 0.055 rad)
why.dynamic: slow-motion test fails (scene is static): see dynamic.motion
why.dynamic.motion: right_return_impulse needs the pendulum still swinging away at > 0.25 rad/s after the paddle leaves it: an impulse, not a slow push
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: excite, brake, return impulse, recover, low-energy hold
why.feedback: braking needs the pendulum's swing to be observed (angular speed < 0.45 rad/s at the touch); its mass and damping are not given

pandadyn/d09_lever_launch_catch_reload.n: Launch, catch and reload a ball
pandadyn/d09_lever_launch_catch_reload.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms share a see-saw launcher: the right arm uses its cup to load a ball into the launcher's basket, the left arm strikes the lever with a mallet to fling the ball into the air, and the right cup catches it. The cycle is repeated, and the ball must finally come to rest in a box sliding on a rail, without the mallet ever touching it.
steps: basket of the passive see-saw launcher, cup moved away
struck with the mallet so the ball is flung into free flight
in the right cup in free flight
launcher basket a second time, cup cleared away
struck again, mallet never touching the ball
open box sliding on a rail, at rest while the box moves

why.articulated: a passive see-saw launcher lever is struck to fling the ball (lever near horizontal when loaded)
why.dynamic: the receiving box slides back and forth on a rail
why.dynamic.motion: the mallet strike must launch the ball into free flight above 0.20 m, and the cup must catch it in flight
why.planning: 6 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: load, launch, catch, reload and clear, launch, retain in moving box
why.feedback: the launched ball's flight must be observed to catch it; object trajectories (launch speeds, restitution and friction are not given in standard mode) must be observed as they unfold
why.transport: load the ball into the launcher basket twice and finally get it to rest in a box sliding on a rail [one ball launched, caught and retained in the moving box]

pandadyn/d10_moving_grasp_handover.n: Hand over a part from a moving conveyor
pandadyn/d10_moving_grasp_handover.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms with plain grippers must take a long bar-shaped part off a running roller conveyor, the left arm grasping it while it moves and lifting it. The left arm then presents it for a hand-over, with both grippers briefly holding it, and the right arm lays it into a long open slot sliding back and forth on a rail.
steps: off the powered conveyor while it is still moving
part held by the left gripper
from the left gripper to the right gripper, both gripping before the left lets go
long open slot sliding on a rail, lying in the slot while it moves

why.dynamic: the part rides a powered conveyor and the slot slides on a rail
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: moving pickup, moving presentation, overlapping grips, donor release, delivery into the moving slot
why.feedback: the conveyor part and the moving slot must be tracked as they move
why.transport: grasp a part from a running conveyor, hand it over between arms and lay it into a moving slot [one part handed over and laid into the moving slot]

pandadyn/d11_moving_fixture_unlock.n: Unlock a moving fixture to release a ball
pandadyn/d11_moving_fixture_unlock.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms must free a ball from a hand-held fixture: the left arm grips the fixture and lifts it off its stand, and while it is still moving the right arm inserts a peg into a socket, presses a latch button until a gate opens, and withdraws. The ball then runs down a fixed chute into a basin, and the fixture must never be dropped.
steps: off its stand by the left gripper, never dropped
square side socket of the still-moving fixture
pushed down with the peg until the gate opens
pulled back out of the socket while the left hand keeps holding the fixture
basin at the foot of the fixed chute, ball running down by itself

why.precision-contact: insert a peg into a socket on the moving fixture (within 5 mm of the axis, 10-35 mm deep)
why.articulated: press the spring-loaded latch button down by more than 17 mm with the peg to open the gate
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: present the moving fixture, insert, unlatch, withdraw while holding, gravity delivery
why.transport: lift the hand-held fixture off its stand, then let its ball run down a chute into a basin [the goal is one ball in the basin; the hand-held fixture is a means]

pandadyn/d12_reciprocal_sliding_transfer.n: Slide a cube between two scoops
pandadyn/d12_reciprocal_sliding_transfer.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms each hold a level, shallow scoop that is open toward the other, and a cube on a very slippery surface starts on the left scoop. Without tilting, the arms must accelerate so that the cube slides onto the right scoop and back, then set it on a fixed output platform at rest, so the cube is moved by inertia and kept in contact with the scoops.
steps: slid out of the left scoop onto the right scoop, at rest, scoops not tilted
slid back from the right scoop onto the left scoop, at rest
fixed output platform, left at rest

why.dynamic: slow-motion test fails (scene is static): see dynamic.motion
why.dynamic.motion: without tilting the scoops (< 2.1 deg), the cube must be made to slide out over the open edge by the scoop's acceleration (inertial slip)
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: slip, receive and brake, reposition, slip back and brake, final deposit
why.feedback: the sliding cube must be received and braked on the other scoop; the surface friction is not given in standard mode
why.transport: transfer a cube from scoop to scoop and back, then deposit it on an output platform [one cube transferred and deposited on the platform]

pandadyn/d13_supported_cube_flip_relay.n: Flip a cube twice on a tray
pandadyn/d13_supported_cube_flip_relay.tldr: Two Franka Panda arms, the left holding a large shallow tray bearing a cube and the right a small flat pusher, must flip the cube over twice so that its original bottom face ends up on top. Each flip is a short push that ends before the cube is half way over, leaving it to complete the tip on its own momentum, and the tray finally carries the cube to an output point.
steps: presentation point, cube never leaving the tray
tipped onto an adjacent face by a short push that ends before half-way
new place for the second tip
second tip so the original bottom face ends on top
output point with the cube correctly oriented

why.precision-contact: tip the cube onto an adjacent face with a push released within a tilt window, twice, so the original bottom face ends on top (pivoting)
why.dynamic: slow-motion test fails (scene is static): see dynamic.motion
why.dynamic.motion: the push must end before the cube is half-way over, so the cube completes the tip on its own momentum
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: present, flip, reposition, flip again, oriented output
why.feedback: the cube's settled pose after the first momentum flip must be observed before the second push
why.transport: carry the cube on the tray to a presentation point, a new place and the output point [one cube carried to the output point]

pandadyn/s01_cup_route_delivery.n: Catch a ball and route it into a cart
pandadyn/s01_cup_route_delivery.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm holding an open cup must catch a ball thrown up at the start, pour it into the designated one of two raised channels, then catch it again in flight after it rolls out and bounces off a tilted plate. It finally puts the ball in a cart sliding along a rail, so timing against two flights and a moving target is critical.
steps: in the open cup after the upward throw
designated one of two raised gravity channels, poured from the cup
in the cup in flight after it leaves the channel and bounces off the rebound plate
cart sliding on a rail, at rest while the cart moves

why.dynamic: the ball is thrown upward at t = 0 and the cart slides back and forth
why.dynamic.motion: two catches of a ball in free flight in a shallow cup (0.028 m walls) with retention
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: catch, route entry, rebound off the plate, downstream catch, moving cart delivery
why.feedback: the thrown ball and its bounce off a very bouncy rebound plate must be observed to catch it; object trajectories (launch speeds, restitution and friction are not given in standard mode) must be observed as they unfold
why.transport: catch the ball, pour it into the designated channel, recatch it and put it into a moving cart [one ball delivered into the moving cart]

pandadyn/s02_plate_catch_transport_relea.n: Catch and carry a ball on a plate
pandadyn/s02_plate_catch_transport_relea.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm holding a flat plate with no rim must catch a ball tossed up at the start, settle it at the plate's centre, carry it through two waypoints that make a turn without it rolling off, and finally tip it into a basin sliding back and forth along a rail. Balancing a rolling ball on a flat surface and releasing it into a moving target are the difficulties.
steps: on the flat rimless plate after the toss
through two waypoints that make a turn without the ball rolling off
settled at the plate centre again after the transport
basin sliding on a rail, tipped off the plate, at rest while the basin moves

why.precision-contact: keep a ball balanced at the centre of a flat rimless plate through a turning transport
why.dynamic: the ball is tossed up at t = 0 and the basin slides on a rail
why.dynamic.motion: catch a free-flying ball on a rimless plate and settle it without it rolling off
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: catch, recenter, transport through a turn, recover, release into the moving basin
why.feedback: the ball's flight and its rolling on the plate must be observed and corrected
why.transport: catch the ball on a plate, carry it through two waypoints and tip it into a basin moving on a rail [one ball released into the moving basin]

pandadyn/s03_clear_gate_hockey.n: Clear a blocker and bank a puck home
pandadyn/s03_clear_gate_hockey.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm with a paddle must strike a puck sliding toward it over an almost frictionless table so that it hits a sliding blocker bar and shoves it aside along its rail. After the puck returns, a second strike must bank it off the long side rail and across the goal line while the blocker is still pushed aside, so both hits need real force and timing.
steps: into the sliding blocker bar, shoving it aside along its rail
second hit after it returns: bank off the long side rail and across the goal line

why.articulated: the puck must push a sliding blocker bar more than 0.065 m along its rail (a prismatic fixture whose displacement is checked)
why.dynamic: a puck slides toward the robot over an almost frictionless table at t = 0
why.dynamic.motion: strikes must drive the puck hard enough to shove the blocker aside, then bank it off the rail across the goal line
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: strike, clear the blocker, recover, strike, bank and goal
why.feedback: the puck's return after the blocker hit must be observed to time the second strike

pandadyn/s04_impact_release_relay.n: Strike a block to release a ball
pandadyn/s04_impact_release_relay.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm with a paddle must strike a small block sliding toward it along a raised deck so that it hits a spring-held latch and swings a gate open, setting free a ball on an inclined chute. The paddle then intercepts the rolling ball, sends it through a narrow passage between two walls, and brings it to rest in a target zone.
steps: into the spring-held gate latch so the gate swings open and the ball is released
intercepted with the paddle after it leaves the chute
through the narrow passage between two walls
target zone beyond the passage, braked to rest with the paddle

why.articulated: the struck cue must hit a spring-held gate latch and swing the gate open more than 0.45 rad
why.dynamic: the cue block is already sliding along the deck at t = 0
why.dynamic.motion: the paddle must strike the cue hard enough to open the gate by impact, then intercept and redirect the rolling ball
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: strike, unlatch, intercept, redirect through the passage, brake in the zone
why.feedback: the released ball's roll down the chute must be observed to intercept it

pandadyn/s05_sliding_receive_align_deliv.n: Receive a sliding cube and move it by inertia
pandadyn/s05_sliding_receive_align_deliv.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm holding a shallow tray open on one side must receive a cube sliding off a slippery lane, then, without tilting the tray, make the cube slide inside it to a staging point just by accelerating. After carrying it through two waypoints, the arm must match the speed of a platform sliding on a rail and get the cube onto it without touching it.
steps: in the shallow tray after it leaves the slippery lane, settled
slid inside the level tray to the staging point by tray acceleration, no tilting
fixed offset from the slowly sliding platform, matching its velocity
onto the moving platform, riding at rest without touching the tray

why.dynamic: the cube slides along a lane at t = 0 and the platform moves on a rail
why.dynamic.motion: inertial staging: with the tray level, a horizontal acceleration > 0.54 m/s^2 must make the cube slide to a staging point within 14 mm
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: receive, inertial staging, transport, velocity matching, support transfer
why.feedback: the arriving cube and the moving platform must be tracked (velocity matching within 0.05 m/s)
why.transport: receive a sliding cube in a tray, carry it through waypoints and transfer it onto a moving platform [one cube transferred onto the moving platform]

pandadyn/s06_cube_flip_route_recover.n: Flip a cube and slide it to a pocket
pandadyn/s06_cube_flip_route_recover.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm with a pusher blade must tip a cube resting on a raised surface so that the face initially toward the robot ends on top, the blade letting go so the cube completes the flip on its own momentum. The blade then pushes the cube onto an inclined chute, meets it near the lower end, and brings it to rest in a pocket with the same face still up.
steps: tipped by a short blade push so the -x face ends on top by its own momentum
onto the inclined chute with the same face still up
met by the blade on its downhill side near the chute's lower end
pocket at the bottom of the chute, at rest with the same face on top

why.precision-contact: tip the cube by a push released within a 1.7-43.9 degree tilt window (pivoting), keeping the face orientation through the chute
why.dynamic: slow-motion test fails (scene is static): see dynamic.motion
why.dynamic.motion: momentum face flip: the cube must complete the tip on its own momentum after the blade lets go
why.planning: 4 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: momentum flip, oriented chute entry, downstream intercept, pocket delivery
why.feedback: the cube sliding down the chute by itself must be met with the blade near the lower end
why.transport: push the flipped cube onto a chute and bring it to rest in the pocket with the right face up [one cube into the pocket]

pandadyn/s07_conveyor_load_brake_unload.n: Move a part from conveyor to dock via carriage
pandadyn/s07_conveyor_load_brake_unload.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm with a gripper must grasp a small part riding a running conveyor, set it on a carriage that is already coasting along a rail, then grab the carriage's vertical handle to stop it with the part still aboard. It finally regrasps the part and sets it in a fixed dock, so almost everything happens on moving objects.
steps: onto the moving carriage, grasped from the running conveyor and released
gripped by its handle and braked to a stop with the part still on it
fixed dock, lifted off the carriage and left at rest

why.articulated: grip the rail carriage's handle and bring the coasting carriage to a stop (< 0.012 m/s)
why.dynamic: a powered conveyor and a coasting carriage move from t = 0
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: moving acquisition, loaded carriage release, handle braking, regrasp, dock deposit
why.feedback: the conveyor part and the coasting carriage must be tracked
why.transport: grasp a part from a running conveyor, set it on a coasting carriage, regrasp it and set it in a dock [one part ends in the dock; the carriage is braked, not placed]

pandadyn/s08_load_switch_recover.n: Load a cart, throw the switch, recover the part
pandadyn/s08_load_switch_recover.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm with a gripper must grasp a small part riding a conveyor, drop it into a cart coasting along a channel, and push a hinged track switch with a finger so that the cart is steered into the branch chosen for this instance. It then grasps the part again and lifts it out of the cart before the cart runs too far, which demands careful timing.
steps: moving cart, grasped from the running conveyor and dropped in
pushed with a finger to steer the cart into the selected branch before it arrives
out of the cart and held up before the cart runs too far down the branch

why.articulated: push a passive hinged track switch with a finger to the selected side before the cart reaches it
why.dynamic: a powered conveyor and a coasting cart move from t = 0
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: pickup, load cart, throw the switch, cart takes the branch, recover the part
why.feedback: the cart's progress must be watched to set the switch in time and recover the part before it runs too far
why.transport: grasp a part from a running conveyor, drop it into a coasting cart and lift it out again [one part recovered from the cart]

pandadyn/s09_toss_recatch_delivery.n: Catch, self-toss and recatch a ball
pandadyn/s09_toss_recatch_delivery.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm holding a shallow cup with one open side must catch a ball thrown high at the start, then toss it straight up out of the cup with a genuine throw and catch it again after moving the cup sideways. It finally releases the ball into a box sliding along a rail, where it must settle while the box is moving.
steps: in the shallow one-sided cup after the high throw
straight up out of the cup at the launch region, leaving the cup floor while rising
in the cup again after moving it sideways
open box sliding on a rail, settled while the box moves

why.dynamic: the ball is thrown at t = 0 and the box slides back and forth
why.dynamic.motion: a real self-toss (ball leaves the cup floor while rising, > 0.2 m/s) followed by a displaced recatch
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: catch, launch region, self-toss, displaced recatch, moving delivery
why.feedback: the thrown and self-tossed ball flights must be observed to catch them
why.transport: catch the ball in the cup and finally release it into a box sliding on a rail [one ball delivered into the moving box]

pandadyn/s10_swinging_load_transit_dock.n: Carry a swinging load past an obstacle
pandadyn/s10_swinging_load_transit_dock.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm must grip a short carrier bar with a pendulum already swinging beneath it and damp the swing by timing its own motion against it. It then carries the bar through two waypoints without letting the bar or pendulum touch a block, damps the leftover swing again, and lowers the bar until the pendulum's ball rests centred in a dock.
steps: gripped with both fingers, pendulum swing damped
through two waypoints without touching the block obstacle
still gripped, residual pendulum swing damped again
dock, centred, swing settled and the bar still gripped

why.articulated: the carrier's hinged pendulum must be settled (|angle| < 0.07 rad, rate < 0.18 rad/s) at three stages
why.dynamic: the pendulum is already swinging at t = 0
why.dynamic.motion: the near-frictionless swing only damps through gripper motion timed against it (active anti-sway); a slow path does not damp it
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: grip and damp, transit A, transit B, cancel residual swing, dock
why.feedback: the swing phase must be observed to damp it
why.transport: grip the carrier bar and carry it through two waypoints past an obstacle until the pendulum bob rests in a dock [one carrier, bob centred in the dock]

pandadyn/s11_cylinder_rescue_route_deliv.n: Rescue a rolling cylinder and deliver it
pandadyn/s11_cylinder_rescue_route_deliv.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm holding a tray open on one side must intercept a short cylinder rolling off the end of a raised lane and bring it to rest lying along a required direction. It then sends the cylinder through a gently sloping guide channel without touching it, catches it again at the exit, and delivers it with the same alignment into a pocket sliding on a rail.
steps: intercepted in the open-sided tray as it runs off the lane
brought to rest in the tray with its long axis along world y
gently sloping guide channel near its entry, then travels out the far end untouched
in the tray at the channel exit, aligned and settled
pocket sliding on a rail, lying along y, at rest while the pocket moves

why.dynamic: the cylinder is rolling at t = 0 and the pocket slides on a rail
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: interception, axial alignment, guide traverse, exit reception, oriented moving delivery
why.feedback: the rolling cylinder and the moving pocket must be tracked
why.transport: intercept a rolling cylinder in the tray, align it, send it through a guide channel, catch it again and deliver it into a moving pocket [one cylinder into the moving pocket]

pandadyn/s12_moving_bridge_puck_relay.n: Send a puck across a spinning bridge
pandadyn/s12_moving_bridge_puck_relay.tldr: A single Franka Panda arm with a paddle must strike a puck sliding along a raised lane so that it crosses a platform spinning continuously about a vertical axis and reaches an exit lane. The paddle then intercepts it, strikes it again and sends it past a hinged, partly open gate and over a goal line without touching it as it crosses and with the gate still open.
steps: from the source lane onto the spinning bridge and on to the exit lane
intercepted with the paddle on the exit lane
along the exit lane past the partly open gate and over the goal line, paddle not touching

why.dynamic: a puck slides toward the paddle at t = 0 and the bridge spins continuously
why.dynamic.motion: two strikes must send the puck across a spinning bridge onto the exit lane and then past a gate across the goal line
why.planning: 5 phases, each enabled by the previous one and checked in order: strike, bridge transfer, interception, second strike, goal while the gate is open
why.feedback: the puck's path over the spinning bridge must be observed to intercept it

bigym2/dishwasher_close.n: Close a dishwasher and its racks
bigym2/dishwasher_close.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must push two pulled-out racks into a dishwasher and then shut its open door. The three parts depend on each other, since both racks have to be in before the door can close, and the humanoid must do it while its whole-body controller keeps it upright.

why.articulated: push the dishwasher's two sliding racks in and close its hinged door (three joints, each within 5% of travel)
why.planning: three dependent closures: both racks must be in before the door can shut

bigym2/dishwasher_load_plates.n: Load plates into a dishwasher rack
bigym2/dishwasher_load_plates.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must take two plates from a dish rack on the counter and stand them on edge in the lower rack of an open dishwasher, then let go so that both stay standing without help. Slotting thin plates upright and gently, without dropping any, makes this a delicate placement task.
steps: dishwasher lower rack, standing on edge

why.arrangement: two plates from the dish rack into the dishwasher's lower rack, standing on edge [both plates must stand in the dishwasher's lower rack at once]

bigym2/drawer_top_open.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must open the top drawer of a kitchen cabinet by pulling it nearly all the way out. It is a single articulated-object pull, but the humanoid must grip the drawer and pull steadily while its whole-body controller keeps it balanced.
steps: out to within 10% of full travel

why.articulated: pull the top drawer out to within 10% of full travel

embodied-olympics-fun/alpine_slalom.tldr: Ski the slalom: one run down the course on your skis, both ski tips and both feet through each of the 32 gates in order, then over the finish line.

embodied-olympics-fun/backflip.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid standing in the middle of an empty, flat exercise floor must do a standing backflip: jump, rotate backwards through a full turn in the air, land on its feet and stand up. The whole rotation has to come from a single brief flight launched from a standing start, so the task needs a powerful, well-timed take-off and a controlled landing without falling.
steps: standing backflip, 300 degrees backward turn in the air, landing on the feet
stand upright on the feet for 2 s

why.locomotion: jump, turn backwards a full turn in the air, land on the feet and stand
why.dynamic: a flip
why.dynamic.motion: a salto: flight with ~9 rad/s rotation

embodied-olympics-fun/badminton_serve.tldr: Serve: standing in your right service court, let the shuttle go from your left hand and hit it with the racket in your right hand, base first and below 1.15 m, over the net into the receiver's service court diagonally opposite.

embodied-olympics-fun/balance_beam.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid starts standing in a one-foot-in-front-of-the-other stance on the near end of a raised gymnastics balance beam and must walk along it to the far end and stand there without anything touching the floor. The beam is narrower than the robot's normal stance, so ordinary walking would put the feet beside it and the gait needs careful balance.
steps: 5 m along the 10 cm wide beam to its far end
stand on the far end of the beam for 2 s

why.locomotion: walk the 5 m, 10 cm-wide beam to the far end and stand

embodied-olympics-fun/balance_board.n: Stay balanced on a roller board
embodied-olympics-fun/balance_board.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands with its feet on a deck that rests on a free-rolling roller and must stay balanced there for a sustained period, with neither end of the deck nor any part of the robot touching the floor. The starting pose is an unstable equilibrium that would run out within seconds if left alone, so continuous corrective control is needed.
steps: upright on the roller board for 30 s, no deck end touching the floor

why.locomotion: stay balanced on a roller board for 30 s with neither end of the deck touching the floor

embodied-olympics-fun/basketball_dribble.n: Dribble a basketball up the court
embodied-olympics-fun/basketball_dribble.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid on a basketball court must dribble a ball with its right hand from the end line across the centre line, walking the whole way without a dribbling or travelling violation. The ball must be repeatedly pushed to the floor and met again on its bounce while the robot keeps walking, so hand timing and gait have to work together.
steps: right-hand dribbles, ball kept within 2 m
14 m up the court across the centre line, no travelling violation

why.locomotion: travel 14 m up the court to the frontcourt with both feet, without travelling violations
why.dynamic: dribbling
why.dynamic.motion: dribble: each palm touch must push the ball to the floor and meet its bounce (<0.3 s contact), timed while walking

embodied-olympics-fun/bowling.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands behind the foul line of a bowling lane with a ball hanging from its right hand and must deliver it down the lane so that all ten pins are knocked down. The pins are very far away, so the ball must be released with enough speed and on a straight line, and the release timing sets both its pace and direction.
steps: down the lane, all ten pins knocked down

why.dynamic: a delivery
why.dynamic.motion: the ball must be delivered at >= ~4 m/s to roll 18 m and strike all ten pins

embodied-olympics-fun/box_jump.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing in front of a tall plyometric box must jump onto it from a two-foot take-off, land on top with both feet and stand up straight. The box rests loose on the floor and can slide or tip if pushed, and a slow, quasi-static motion cannot leave the ground, so the jump needs real take-off power and a stable landing.
steps: two-foot take-off onto the 0.61 m box, both feet landing on top
stand up straight on the box for 2 s

why.locomotion: two-foot jump onto a 0.61 m box, land on top and stand
why.dynamic: a jump
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground (touching the box before the jump fails)

embodied-olympics-fun/boxing.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid facing a hanging heavy bag must punch it once with the knuckles of its right fist on a marked band, hard enough to give it a required push, then bring the fist back to guard and stand. A shove or slap does not count, so the task needs a short, fast blow with good aim and a controlled recovery.
steps: one right-fist knuckle punch inside the marked band, impulse of 12 N s
back to guard, within 0.35 m of the right shoulder
at guard while standing for 2 s

why.dynamic: a punch
why.dynamic.motion: a blow of <= 0.1 s giving the 30 kg bag >= 12 N s: a push is refused

embodied-olympics-fun/breaking_windmill.tldr: Breaking: go down to the floor and do three consecutive windmills, rolling over your upper back, shoulders and chest while your legs circle round above the floor.

embodied-olympics-fun/catch.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing on a level field must catch a baseball that is launched from far away and comes down steeply near it, gripping the ball with a hand before it touches the ground or the body and holding on. The landing spot is not fixed, so the robot has to observe the flight and get a hand there in time.
steps: gripped by a hand before touching the ground or body
kept in the hand for 1 s

why.dynamic: scene: a fly ball launched 40 m away; motion: a catch
why.dynamic.motion: a hand must reach the falling ball (16.6 m/s) in time and grip it
why.feedback: the ball's landing point (somewhere within 3 m) has to be observed during its flight

embodied-olympics-fun/catch_and_shoot.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid at the top of the key of a basketball court must catch a chest pass thrown to it from the left wing and then shoot from where it stands so that the ball drops into the basket from above. It combines receiving a fast, moving ball with an accurate throw, and the incoming pass has to be observed to place the catch.
steps: chest pass gripped before it touches the floor
shot into the basket from above, from where it stands

why.dynamic: scene: a chest pass comes from the wing; motion: catch then shoot
why.dynamic.motion: catching a 7.2 m/s pass and a jump-free shot released at ~8.7 m/s
why.feedback: the incoming pass has to be observed to catch it

embodied-olympics-fun/clean_and_jerk.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing over a barbell on a lifting platform must lift it to its shoulders, then to locked arms overhead, and hold it motionless there until the down signal. The weight is too heavy for the arm joints alone, so the lift depends on driving with the legs and keeping balance under a heavy load.
steps: from the platform to the shoulders, legs extended, motionless
overhead and motionless until the down signal

why.locomotion: whole-body lift with leg drive, straight knees and feet in line, held motionless overhead
why.dynamic: an explosive lift
why.dynamic.motion: slowly, curling 45 kg to the shoulders needs 34 N m of an 18 N m elbow: the clean and the jerk need leg-driven momentum
why.transport: lift the 45 kg barbell from the platform to the shoulders, then to locked arms overhead [one barbell lifted overhead and held]

embodied-olympics-fun/crawl.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid starting upright must get down under a course of low wires strung lower than its hips, and crawl the whole length until its entire body is past the last wire, without touching any wire. It must change from walking to a prone crawl and then keep its body low and clear of a long series of wires.
steps: prone crawl under 21 wires over 10 m, whole body past the last wire

why.locomotion: crawl prone under 21 wires 0.45 m high along 10 m without touching one

embodied-olympics-fun/discus.n: Throw a discus from the circle
embodied-olympics-fun/discus.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid inside a throwing circle must throw the discus held in its right hand so that it lands inside the marked sector at a required minimum distance, then leave the circle through its rear half and stand. It needs a fast whole-body throw while staying inside the circle, and a release that sends the discus the right way.
steps: lands in the sector at least 15 m from the circle
out of the circle through its rear half

why.locomotion: a whole-body throw from the circle, then leave it from its rear half and stand
why.dynamic: a throw
why.dynamic.motion: the discus must land 15 m away: released at ~13 m/s

embodied-olympics-fun/dodgeball.tldr: Dodge: five cloth dodgeballs are thrown at you by ball machines that aim at you; do not let a live ball touch you, stay inside your court and on your feet.

embodied-olympics-fun/double_dutch.tldr: Jump Double Dutch: enter the two ropes turning in opposite directions and jump them 10 times in a row, one rope per jump, without a rope ever touching you, then land on your feet.

embodied-olympics-fun/dribble_slalom.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid on a grass pitch must dribble a football out through a line of six cones, round the last one and back through them over the start line, keeping the ball close and touching no cone. Each cone must be passed on the side shown by a mark, and the ball must be tapped and met again as it rolls free.
steps: taps that keep the ball rolling within 2 m, no hand contact
slalom out through six cones and back over the start line, each cone on its marked side

why.locomotion: walk/run the slalom out through six cones and back, the pelvis passing each on the prescribed side
why.dynamic: football dribbling
why.dynamic.motion: dribbling: the ball is advanced by taps that send it rolling free and must be met again (the codebook names dribble), keeping it within 2 m
why.planning: 12 ordered gates, each passed on a given side by both the ball and the robot

embodied-olympics-fun/dunk.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing under a basketball hoop with the ball in its right hand must jump, force the ball down through the ring from above with its hand on it, and land on its feet. The ring is higher than the robot can normally reach, so the jump needs real take-off power and a controlled landing.
steps: take off under the basket from the floor
forced down through the ring from above with the hand on it
land on the feet and stand for 1 s

why.locomotion: jump, force the ball down through the ring and land on the feet
why.dynamic: a dunk
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground (0.7 m of rise above the standing reach)

embodied-olympics-fun/dunk_between_legs.tldr: From the top of the key, with the basketball held in your two hands, dribble it, make one of its bounces pass between your legs, gather it in both hands, and with at most two steps dunk it: force it down through the ring from above with your hands on it, then land on your feet.

embodied-olympics-fun/first_time_shot.tldr: Shoot first time: the football rolls down a ramp and across in front of you; with one touch of a foot send it into the official goal 11 m away.

embodied-olympics-fun/free_kick_wall.tldr: Take a direct free kick: with one kick of a foot, send the ball over or around the wall of mannequins into the official goal 20.0 m away.

embodied-olympics-fun/free_throw.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing just behind the free-throw line of a basketball court must throw the ball held in its right hand so that it enters the basket from above. A shot that drops through the ring needs the ball to leave the hand at the right speed and angle, so the task is mainly about a precise, repeatable throwing motion while staying balanced.
steps: into the basket from above, from behind the free-throw line

why.dynamic: a shot
why.dynamic.motion: a throw: the ball must leave the hand at ~8 m/s at the right angle to drop through the ring

embodied-olympics-fun/freeski_360.tldr: Drop in from the start platform, ride the in-run, take off from the kicker, do a 360 in the air, land on your skis and ride away past the finish line.

embodied-olympics-fun/freeski_straight_a.tldr: Drop in from the start platform, ride the in-run, take off from the kicker, do a straight air in the air, land on your skis and ride away past the finish line.

embodied-olympics-fun/giant_slalom.tldr: Ski the giant slalom: one run down the course on your skis, both ski tips and both feet through each of the 26 gates in order, then over the finish line.

embodied-olympics-fun/goalkeeper_save.tldr: Keep goal: three penalty kicks are shot at the official goal you stand in; keep every ball out, with a foot on the goal line at each kick.

embodied-olympics-fun/golf_putt.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid standing side-on on a putting green must hole a putt of a few metres, using one stroke of a putter held in its right hand to roll a golf ball across in front of its feet into the hole. The putter strike has to be a brief tap with the right speed and direction, since a push or a second stroke does not count.
steps: one putter stroke rolling it 3 m into the hole

why.dynamic: a putt
why.dynamic.motion: a stroke whose contacts last at most 0.03 s must roll the ball 3 m into the hole: an impulse, a push fails

embodied-olympics-fun/handstand.tldr: Do a handstand: from your stance get up onto your hands, hold the handstand still for 2 s with only your hands on the floor, then come back down onto your feet and stand.

embodied-olympics-fun/header.n: Head a crossed football into goal
embodied-olympics-fun/header.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing at the edge of the goal area must meet a football crossed from the wing with its head and send it into the goal past a goalkeeper dummy. The ball arrives at head height from the side after a delay, so the robot has to watch its flight, time a whole-body lunge, and use its head as the striking surface.
steps: headed into the goal past the keeper dummy

why.locomotion: meet the cross with the head: a whole-body lunge, the body itself is the striking surface
why.dynamic: scene: a cross from the wing; motion: a header
why.dynamic.motion: the ball must leave the head faster than it came: a timed lunge strike
why.feedback: the cross's flight has to be observed to meet it

embodied-olympics-fun/high_bar_swing.n: Giant swing on the high bar
embodied-olympics-fun/high_bar_swing.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid hanging by both hands from a gymnastics high bar must perform one giant swing, taking its extended body in a full circle around the bar without letting go. Nothing holds the legs up, so the swing must be built up from below the bar with whole-body momentum and carried over the top while the grip holds.
steps: one giant swing, a full 360 degree circle round the high bar with body extended

why.locomotion: hanging by both hands, take the extended body through a full giant swing round the bar
why.dynamic: a giant swing
why.dynamic.motion: the swing must be built up below the bar and carried over the top with an extended body: needs momentum

embodied-olympics-fun/high_jump.n: Run up and clear the high jump
embodied-olympics-fun/high_jump.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid starts well back on a runway and must approach a high-jump bar, take off from one foot, go over the bar between the uprights without knocking it off, and come down on the landing mat. It combines a running approach with a powerful one-foot take-off, and a quasi-static motion cannot leave the ground.
steps: one-foot take-off over the 1.0 m bar without knocking it off, onto the mat

why.locomotion: approach, take off from one foot and clear the bar onto the mat
why.dynamic: a jump
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground (one-foot take-off)

embodied-olympics-fun/hurdles_freestandi.tldr: Run the 50 m hurdles over four free-standing hurdles: go over each one in your lane, never beside it, under its top, or after pushing it away, leave at least one of them standing, and bring your torso to the finish line.

embodied-olympics-fun/inline_slalom.tldr: Skate the speed slalom: from the start box, 12 m of run-up, then on one foot through the 20 cones, passing them alternately left and right, and over the end line, as fast as you can.

embodied-olympics-fun/javelin.n: Throw a javelin over the shoulder
embodied-olympics-fun/javelin.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid on a javelin runway must throw the javelin held in its right hand over the shoulder so that its head strikes the ground first, inside the marked sector at a required distance, then leave the runway behind the arc and stand. It needs a powerful whole-body throw with the right release timing, while staying behind the throwing line.
steps: over the shoulder, head lands first in the sector at least 20 m from the arc
off the runway behind the arc

why.locomotion: a whole-body over-the-shoulder throw from the runway, then leave the runway behind the arc and stand
why.dynamic: a throw
why.dynamic.motion: the javelin must fly 20 m: released at ~14-15 m/s

embodied-olympics-fun/juggle_three.n: Juggle three balls in a cascade
embodied-olympics-fun/juggle_three.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid standing on level ground with a ball resting on each forearm must juggle three balls in a cascade, throwing each ball in an arc from one hand to the other and catching it, until a long run of catches has been made without a drop. All three balls are in the air at once, so the throws and catches must keep a steady rhythm.
steps: arcs from hand to hand in a cascade, each rising at least 0.3 m
gripped by the other hand, ten catches in a row

why.dynamic: scene: the third ball is launched by the venue at t = 2 s; motion: a three-ball cascade
why.dynamic.motion: throws rising >= 0.3 m and catches within 0.15 s of touch, ten in a row
why.feedback: three balls in flight must be tracked to place each catch

embodied-olympics-fun/juggling.n: Keep a football up with feet
embodied-olympics-fun/juggling.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid standing on grass must drop a football from its hand and keep it in the air for a run of consecutive touches using its feet, legs or head, without letting it reach the ground or touch a hand again. Each touch must be an active strike that sends the ball back up, so the robot has to balance, sometimes on one foot, while placing the ball.
steps: kept in the air by feet, legs or head for ten touches

why.locomotion: keep a football up with feet, legs and head for ten touches while standing (on one foot when needed)
why.dynamic: keepie-uppie
why.dynamic.motion: each touch must send the ball off with >= 0.95 of its arrival speed and rise 0.22 m: active strikes, not a still limb

embodied-olympics-fun/juggling_feet.tldr: Juggle the football with your feet: drop it from between your palms and keep it in the air for ten foot touches in a row, each one sending the ball up above your knees, without it touching the ground or any other part of you.

embodied-olympics-fun/juggling_head.tldr: Juggle the football on your head: a ball machine in front of you lobs it onto your head; keep it in the air with ten headers in a row, touching it with nothing but your head, without it touching the ground.

embodied-olympics-fun/jump_rope.tldr: Skip rope: turn the rope forwards with both hands, over your head and under your feet, and jump it with both feet together, 17 times within one minute.

embodied-olympics-fun/kick_target.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands in front of a hanging heavy bag and must deliver one hard kick with its right foot or shin onto a marked band at trunk height, then settle back onto both feet. The blow has to be sharp and short rather than a slow push, which demands balancing on one leg while swinging the other.
steps: one right foot or shin kick inside the marked band, impulse of 20 N s
stand on both feet for 2 s after the kick

why.locomotion: kick the bag with the right foot or shin, balancing on one leg, then stand on both feet
why.dynamic: a kick
why.dynamic.motion: a blow of <= 0.15 s giving the bag >= 20 N s: a push is refused

embodied-olympics-fun/layup.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid holds a basketball in its right hand inside the restricted area of a basketball court and must take a couple of steps toward the basket, jump, and let the ball go in the air close to the ring so it drops in from above. The steps are limited and the release must happen mid-flight, so run-up, take-off and release have to be timed together.
steps: at most two steps towards the basket, then take-off
released in the air within 1.25 m of the ring, entering the basket from above

why.locomotion: at most two steps towards the basket, jump and release in the air
why.dynamic: a layup
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground; the ball is released in the air

embodied-olympics-fun/long_jump.n: Long jump into a sand pit
embodied-olympics-fun/long_jump.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid starts far back on a runway and must run up, take off from behind the take-off line, fly over the gap beyond it and land inside the sand pit. The jump must be a real flight rather than a fall, the takeoff may not overstep the line, and the landing on soft sand must stay stable.
steps: 20 m run-up along the runway to the take-off line
take-off behind the line, flight over the metre beyond it, landing in the sand pit

why.locomotion: run up and jump from behind the take-off line into the sand pit
why.dynamic: a running jump
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground after a run-up

embodied-olympics-fun/long_rope.tldr: Jump the long rope: standing in the middle of a rope turned by two rope-turning machines, jump it 10 times in a row, the rope passing under both your feet while you are in the air, without the rope ever touching you.

embodied-olympics-fun/paddle_bounce.n: Keep a ball bouncing on a paddle
embodied-olympics-fun/paddle_bounce.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid with a table tennis paddle fixed to its right hand must keep a dropped table tennis ball bouncing on the paddle for a long run of consecutive bounces, each one returning the ball to about the height it fell from. Every bounce is an active upward hit, so the robot has to watch the ball and place the paddle precisely each time.
steps: bounced on the paddle back to the 1.2 m drop height, 20 in a row

why.dynamic: scene: the ball is dropped in front of the robot; motion: repeated hits
why.dynamic.motion: 20 bounces in a row, each back up to the drop height: every bounce is an active upward hit
why.feedback: each bounce's ball state must be observed to place the next hit

embodied-olympics-fun/penalty_kick.n: Take a penalty kick past the keeper
embodied-olympics-fun/penalty_kick.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands a few steps behind the penalty mark and must walk up and kick the football into the goal with a single kick, past a goalkeeper dummy that slides sideways to cut off the shot. Beating the keeper takes a fast, well-aimed strike rather than a gentle push, all while balancing on the standing leg.
steps: one foot kick from the mark into the goal past the sliding keeper dummy

why.locomotion: walk up 3 m and strike the ball with a foot while balancing on the other leg
why.dynamic: scene: the goalkeeper dummy slides after the kick; motion: a kick
why.dynamic.motion: beating the keeper needs ~12 m/s of ball speed from one kick: a strike, not a push

embodied-olympics-fun/pitch_target.n: Pitch a baseball for a strike
embodied-olympics-fun/pitch_target.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands on a pitcher's mound with a baseball in its right hand and must throw it, in the air all the way, through the strike zone above home plate far ahead. The throw needs a fast, accurately aimed release from the hand while the body stays on the plate, so speed and aim must be coordinated.
steps: on the fly through the strike zone over home plate, foot on the plate

why.dynamic: a pitch
why.dynamic.motion: throw the baseball through the strike zone on the fly (~14-22 m/s)

embodied-olympics-fun/platform_10m.tldr: Do a forward dive straight (101A) from the 10 m platform: from your standing start at its front end, take off, turn half a somersault forwards in the straight position and enter the water head first, vertical, with your arms stretched beyond your head.

embodied-olympics-fun/pole_vault.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid carries a rigid pole down a runway and must plant its tip in the box, swing off the ground hanging on it, clear the bar between the uprights without knocking it down, and come down on the mat. Without enough run-up momentum from the plant the robot never leaves the ground, so a long, fast sequence of phases has to be timed together.
steps: 10 m run-up carrying the pole to the box
into the box at the end of the runway
swing off the ground hanging on the pole, over the 2.00 m bar, onto the mat with the bar still on its pegs

why.tool-use: plant the carried pole's tip in the box and swing up on it
why.locomotion: leave the ground hanging on the pole, go over the bar and come down on the mat
why.dynamic: a vault
why.dynamic.motion: the take-off and swing over a 2.00 m bar need momentum from the plant; slowly the robot never leaves the ground

embodied-olympics-fun/round_off.tldr: Do a round-off: go from your feet onto your hands, turn half round through the handstand and come down onto both feet together facing back the way you came, then stand.

embodied-olympics-fun/rugby_conversion.tldr: Kick a conversion: with one place kick of a foot, send the rugby ball standing on its tee over the crossbar and between the posts.

embodied-olympics-fun/shot_put.n: Put a shot from a circle
embodied-olympics-fun/shot_put.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands in a throwing circle with a heavy shot held at its neck and must push it from the shoulder with one hand so it lands inside the marked sector at a good distance, then step out of the circle through its rear half and stand. The shot is heavy and must be put rather than slung, so the whole body has to contribute while the hand stays in the legal position.
steps: put from the shoulder with one hand, lands in the sector at least 6 m from the circle
out of the circle through its rear half

why.locomotion: a whole-body put from the circle, then leave it from its rear half and stand
why.dynamic: a put
why.dynamic.motion: the 7.26 kg shot must land 6 m away: released at ~8 m/s

embodied-olympics-fun/shuttle_run.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands behind a start line on a sports floor and must run to a far line and back, twice over, planting a foot beyond the line at each turn, as fast as it can. The qualifying time is below what a walking gait reaches, so the robot has to run and make quick, stable turns without falling.
steps: 4 x 10 m shuttle between two lines, a foot beyond the line at each turn, within 30 s

why.locomotion: run 4 x 10 m with a foot beyond the line at each of three turns
why.dynamic: a timed shuttle run
why.dynamic.motion: the 30 s limit is below what the walking gait reaches (~33 s): running with fast turns is required

embodied-olympics-fun/skateboard_ollie.tldr: Ollie the skateboard from a standstill: pop the tail, take the board up with your feet until all of it is at least 0.05 m off the ground, land on it and stand still on it for 1.0 s.

embodied-olympics-fun/slalom.n: Run an agility course round cones
embodied-olympics-fun/slalom.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid starts beside the start cone of an agility course and must run the prescribed route: around the far corner cones, back to the start line, weaving up and down through the four centre cones, and across the finish, without touching a cone. The route is a sequence of gates passed on given sides, and the time limit forces running with sharp turns instead of a walk.
steps: Illinois agility course round and weaving between the cones in the prescribed order without touching one

why.locomotion: run the Illinois agility course round and between the cones without touching one
why.dynamic: a timed agility run
why.dynamic.motion: the 60 s limit against ~127 s for a walk of the path: running with sharp turns is required
why.planning: a prescribed route of 12 gates in order, each cone passed on a given side, has to be planned as a path

embodied-olympics-fun/sled_push.tldr: Push the weighted sled with your palms on its two upright handles until the whole sled is over the line 12.5 m ahead, within 60 s.

embodied-olympics-fun/snowboard.tldr: Ride the parallel slalom on your snowboard: one run down the course, the board and both feet through each of the 18 gates in order, then over the finish line.

embodied-olympics-fun/springboard_3m.tldr: Do a forward dive straight (101A) from the 3 m springboard: from your standing start at its end, take off from both feet, turn half a somersault forwards in the straight position and enter the water head first, vertical, with your arms stretched beyond your head.

embodied-olympics-fun/sprint.n: Sprint a short race on the starter's lamp
embodied-olympics-fun/sprint.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid waits in its lane at the start line of a short running track and must sprint straight down the lane until its torso crosses the finish line. The starter's gun is replaced by a lamp that turns red, yellow, then green, so the robot must watch it and leave only on green, and the qualifying time requires running rather than walking.
steps: wait for green before leaving, no false start
sprint 50 m down the lane until the torso crosses the finish line within 30 s

why.locomotion: run the 50 m in your lane until the torso crosses the finish line
why.dynamic: a sprint: the run must finish within 30 s of the gun
why.dynamic.motion: the 30 s qualifying time needs a mean of 1.7 m/s, beyond the 0.6 m/s walk: running is required
why.perception: the start is shown only by a start lamp's colour (red/yellow/green) in the cameras
why.feedback: the gun's moment is fixed but not announced: the start must be timed on the lamp turning green (a start before it is a false start)

embodied-olympics-fun/standing_long_jump.n: Standing long jump from a line
embodied-olympics-fun/standing_long_jump.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands with its feet just behind a take-off line and must jump forward off both feet without a step, land at least its own height beyond the line, and then stay standing. The jump needs a genuine flight phase from a standstill, and the landing is judged by the nearest contact, so a stumble or a hand put down shortens the jump.
steps: two-foot take-off without a step, landing on the feet at least 1.32 m beyond the line
stand on the feet for 1 s after landing

why.locomotion: two-foot standing jump at least the robot's height forward, then stand
why.dynamic: a jump
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground

embodied-olympics-fun/steeplechase.n: Clear a hurdle and water pit
embodied-olympics-fun/steeplechase.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid starts on a track and must run up to a hip-high steeplechase hurdle, get over it and the dry water pit behind it, climb out beyond the pit's far edge and finish standing. The sequence of obstacles needs a long stride and a controlled landing on the sloping pit floor, with no stumbling.
steps: 10 m run-up to the steeplechase hurdle
over the 0.914 m hurdle, pelvis and feet above the bar
through the dry water pit and out beyond its far edge
stand on the feet for 1 s beyond the pit

why.locomotion: go over the hip-high steeplechase hurdle and the water pit, get out and stand

embodied-olympics-fun/sumo.tldr: Win a sumo bout: force the opponent robot out of the ring, or make any part of it other than its feet touch the ground, before the same happens to you.

embodied-olympics-fun/sweeper_jump.tldr: Jump the sweeper: standing on your podium, jump over the padded boom each time it sweeps round, 3 times in a row without being hit, then stand still on the podium.

embodied-olympics-fun/table_tennis_retur.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands at one end of a table with a paddle on its right hand and must hit a served table tennis ball, after its first bounce on the robot's side, so that it lands on the opponent's side. The ball is within reach for only a very short moment and arrives with spin, so it must be tracked after the bounce and met with a timed swing.
steps: returned after its bounce so it lands on the opponent's court

why.dynamic: scene: a real served ball; motion: a stroke
why.dynamic.motion: the ball is in reach for 0.14 s and must be struck onto the opponent's court
why.feedback: the serve must be observed after its bounce to meet it

embodied-olympics-fun/taekwondo_kick.tldr: Kick the trunk protector of the dummy in front of you once with a foot, hard enough to score, then land and stand still for 2.0 s.

embodied-olympics-fun/tennis_return.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid waits as the receiver on a tennis court with a racket on its right hand and must hit a served ball, after it bounces in the service box, back over the net into the far singles court. The return calls for a powerful, timed swing, and the robot has to read the serve's bounce and move a few metres sideways to get to the ball in time.
steps: about 3 m sideways to the served ball's bounce
returned after its bounce, over the net into the far singles court

why.dynamic: scene: a 30 m/s serve; motion: a stroke
why.dynamic.motion: the return needs ~24 m/s off the strings: a timed swing
why.feedback: the serve's bounce and path must be observed; the robot has to move ~3 m sideways in time

embodied-olympics-fun/tennis_serve.n: Serve a tennis ball into the box
embodied-olympics-fun/tennis_serve.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands behind the baseline of a tennis court with a ball in its left hand and a racket on its right and must toss the ball, hit it before it lands, and send it over the net into the diagonally opposite service box. Only one serve is allowed, and even the gentlest legal serve needs a fast racket swing timed to the falling toss.
steps: toss up from the left hand, clear of the body
racket hit before it lands, over the net into the diagonal service box

why.dynamic: toss and serve
why.dynamic.motion: the slowest legal serve needs ~12 m/s: a racket swing timed to a falling toss

embodied-olympics-fun/toes_to_bar.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid hangs from a high horizontal bar by both hands and must repeatedly swing its feet up to touch the bar between its hands and return to a full hang each time, without letting go. Nothing holds the legs up, so the swinging legs and arms must be coordinated to repeat the movement several times.
steps: touch the bar between the hands, then back to a full hang, five times, without letting go

why.locomotion: hanging from the bar, bring both feet up to touch it and return to a full hang, five times

embodied-olympics-fun/trampoline.tldr: On the trampoline, bounce as you like, then do one tuck jump, land on both feet, stop the bounce (one more straight out-bounce at most) and stand still.

embodied-olympics-fun/trap_ball.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands on grass while a football is passed along the ground past it and must stop the ball with a foot on first touch, bringing it to rest close to itself within a few moments. A still foot would just send the ball away, so the foot has to yield at the right instant while the robot balances on one leg, and the pass must be tracked as it arrives.
steps: first touch with a foot, brought to rest within 1 m of the robot inside 3 s

why.locomotion: take the pass with a foot and bring the ball to rest within a metre, staying up on one leg
why.dynamic: scene: a pass rolls in at ~6-8 m/s; motion: a cushioning first touch
why.dynamic.motion: a still foot sends the ball off at 5 m/s: the foot must give with the ball at the right instant (a catch with the foot)
why.feedback: the incoming pass has to be observed to meet it

embodied-olympics-fun/triple_jump.n: Triple jump into a sand pit
embodied-olympics-fun/triple_jump.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid starts far back on a runway and must run up, hop from behind the take-off line landing on the same foot, step onto the other foot, and jump from it into the sand pit. Three separate flights are required, with only the supporting foot touching down between them, so each take-off and landing must be controlled to avoid sliding or falling.
steps: 20 m run-up along the runway to the take-off line
hop, step and jump in order, each a flight, the last into the sand pit

why.locomotion: run up, hop, step and jump into the sand pit
why.dynamic: three jumps from a run-up
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground three times

embodied-olympics-fun/vault.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid starts at the end of a long run-up and must run to a springboard, vault over a shoulder-high vault table touching it only with its hands, land on its feet on the mat and stand. The robot needs run-up momentum to flip its body over the table, and the board moves on a spring, so contact, flight and landing must all be timed.
steps: vault over the 1.35 m table touching it only with the hands, onto the landing mat
stand on the feet on the mat for 1 s

why.locomotion: run up and vault over the 1.35 m table with only the hands on it, land and stand
why.dynamic: a vault
why.dynamic.motion: a handspring over the table: flight and rotation need run-up momentum

embodied-olympics-fun/vertical_jump.n: Vertical jump to touch a vane
embodied-olympics-fun/vertical_jump.tldr: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands under a measuring stand and must jump straight up off both feet from a standstill, touch the vane above it with a hand at the top of the jump, then land on its feet and stay standing. The jump has to leave the floor for a real flight without any step, and the hand must reach high enough at the right moment.
steps: straight up off both feet from a standstill without a step
touch the vane above at the top of the jump
land on the feet and stand for 1 s

why.locomotion: jump off both feet, touch the vane above at the top of the jump, land and stand
why.dynamic: a jump
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground

embodied-olympics-fun/volley_shot.n: Volley a crossed ball into goal
embodied-olympics-fun/volley_shot.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands at the penalty mark while a football is crossed in from the wing and must strike it with a foot before it touches the ground, sending it into the goal past a goalkeeper dummy. The ball comes in steeply from the side and must leave faster than it arrived, so the kick must be aimed and timed on a flying ball while balancing on the other leg.
steps: volleyed with a foot before it lands, into the goal past the keeper dummy

why.locomotion: strike the crossed ball with a foot before it lands, balancing on the other leg
why.dynamic: scene: a cross from the wing; motion: a volley
why.dynamic.motion: a volley: the ball must leave faster than it came (a still leg slows it), timed to a ball in flight
why.feedback: the cross's flight has to be observed to meet it

embodied-olympics-fun/volleyball_bump.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands in a volleyball court while an opposing serve comes over the net and must pass it with its forearms in a single short contact, sending it above net height into the setter's target at the net. The serve is a floating ball that falls steeply to one side, so the robot has to track it and get its forearms underneath at the right moment.
steps: forearm pass in one contact, above net height into the setter's target

why.dynamic: scene: a float serve comes over the net; motion: a forearm pass
why.dynamic.motion: a single <0.1 s forearm contact must send the ball above net height into the setter's target: a timed hit
why.feedback: the served ball's flight has to be observed to be under it

embodied-olympics-fun/volleyball_serve.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands behind the end line of a volleyball court with the ball on its left fist and must toss it, then hit it with one hand or arm over the net into the opponent's court. The ball has to be clear of the robot before the hit and the toss may not be a throw, so the hit must be timed to a falling ball and carry it far enough.
steps: toss out of the left hand, clear of the robot, not thrown
hit with one hand or arm over the net into the opponent's court

why.dynamic: toss and serve
why.dynamic.motion: toss the ball and hit it in flight over the net into the court (reference releases ~11 m/s)

embodied-olympics-fun/volleyball_set.n: Set a volleyball for a hitter
embodied-olympics-fun/volleyball_set.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands near the net of a volleyball court while a tossed ball comes down above it and must set it with a single overhead contact of its hands, sending it more than a metre above the net into the outside hitter's target along the net. The contact must be brief and above the head, and the ball's arrival has to be observed to place the hands correctly.
steps: one overhead hand contact, more than 1 m above the net into the hitter's target

why.dynamic: scene: a pass comes down above the robot; motion: an overhead set
why.dynamic.motion: one overhead hand contact must send the ball a metre above the net into the hitter's target: a timed hit
why.feedback: the incoming pass has to be observed

embodied-olympics-fun/volleyball_spike.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands at the attack line of a volleyball court while a set ball comes down near the net and must jump and hit it with a hand above net height, driving it down into the opponent's court, then land on its feet without touching the net. The jump has to be timed to the falling ball, and the strike must point downward, not just forward.
steps: timed take-off to the falling set ball without touching the net
hand hit above net height, driven down into the opponent's court
land on the feet and stand for 1 s

why.locomotion: jump, strike above the net and land on the feet without touching the net
why.dynamic: scene: a set comes down near the net; motion: a jump spike
why.dynamic.motion: the referee requires a flight phase (take-off, airborne, landing): a quasi-static path cannot leave the ground, and the ball is struck down at the apex
why.feedback: the set ball has to be observed to time the jump

embodied-olympics-fun/wall_ball.n: Throw at a wall target and catch
embodied-olympics-fun/wall_ball.tldr: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands behind a line facing a wall with a tennis ball in its right hand and must throw the ball at a target circle on the wall, then catch the rebound with a hand before it touches the ground and keep hold of it. The throw must be fast and accurate, and the catch needs the hand in the right place when the ball returns.
steps: at the target circle on the wall
rebound gripped by a hand before it touches the ground
kept in the hand for 1 s

why.dynamic: throw and catch
why.dynamic.motion: throw at 16-20 m/s to hit the wall target, then catch the rebound before it lands

embodied-olympics-match/badminton_duelrl.tldr: A Franka Panda arm with a racket, mounted on a sliding gantry, plays a singles badminton game on a scaled-down court against a built-in opponent driven by a learned policy. The player sees only camera images and the game runs slowed down, while the opponent reads the true shuttle state, so each return needs quick perception and a well-timed stroke.

gantry to under each incoming shuttle
return over the net into the opponent's court

return over the net into the opponent's court

embodied-olympics-match/fencing_bout_i02.n: Epee fencing bout against scripted fencer
embodied-olympics-match/fencing_bout_i02.tldr: Two Unitree G1 humanoids with real epees fence a direct-elimination bout, played out one short phrase at a time. For each phrase the player picks a tactical intention such as a lunge, a counter-attack or a retreat, against a stronger scripted fencer of the second level that reads those choices. The player works from camera images and has to plan a whole bout rather than a single exchange.

valid touch with the epee point (lunge, stop-hit, counter-attack)

embodied-olympics-match/foosball_match_i.tldr: A motorised foosball table with four rods for one team, driven by slide and rotation commands, plays a game against a scripted computer team of the third level under tournament rules. The player sees the table only through an overhead camera and the game runs in slowed real time, so the program must track a fast ball, time its shots, and respect limits on how long a rod may hold the ball.

embodied-olympics-match/soccer_match.tldr: An agent commands two Booster T1 humanoids as a team in a soccer match against a scripted opposing team on a small boarded pitch, trying to score more goals over two halves. The robots see only through their head cameras, so the ball, teammates, opponents and goals must be told apart visually, and the game keeps running while the agent thinks, pausing only briefly after each point for a review.
steps: found and told apart from the head cameras
to the ball and into position on the 10 x 7 m pitch
swing-leg kick into the opposing goal, pass or shot

why.navigation: move two Booster T1s around a 10 x 7 m pitch to the ball and the goals
why.dynamic: scene: an opposing team and a moving ball; motion: kicks
why.dynamic.motion: goals come from swing-leg kicks timed to the ball
why.perception: only the robots' head cameras: the ball, teammates, opponents and which goal is whose must be found and told apart
why.planning: a 2 v 2 match: coordinate two robots and play against a scripted team over two halves
why.feedback: opponents and the ball move; the play must react to them

embodied-olympics-match/soccerssl_match_.tldr: An agent commands a team of five small omnidirectional wheeled soccer robots against an opposing team on a Small Size League field, trying to score more goals over two halves. It sees the game through shared overhead cameras with a delay and issues move, kick and dribble commands, so passing, shooting and defending must be planned in real time. In this instance the opponent is a stronger team whose robots are steered by a learned network.
steps: to poses around the 9 x 6 m field, to the ball and into position
flat or chipped kick, pass or shot into the opposing goal

why.navigation: drive five omnidirectional robots around the field

why.motion: flat and chipped kicks timed to the ball's arrival
why.planning: a 5 v 5 match: team strategy for five robots against an opposing team
why.feedback: opponents and the ball move; the play must react to them

embodied-olympics-match/tabletennis_duel.n: Table tennis duel against a learned player
embodied-olympics-match/tabletennis_duel.tldr: A Franka Panda arm with a paddle, mounted on a rail so it can slide along the end of the table, plays a table tennis game against a built-in opponent robot that uses a learned policy. Only camera images and the arm's own state are available, and play is slowed but never waits, so the agent must track the fast ball, return it, and review the game between points.
steps: legal serve from the toss device, struck as it falls
rail base to each incoming ball
return onto the opponent's half of the table

why.dynamic: scene: a built-in learned opponent and a ball in play; motion: strikes
why.motion: every return is a timed hit of a ball in flight
why.feedback: the learned opponent's shots must be observed (cameras only) and answered in real time

In this instance the opponent is a strong high-level player, and the match must be started within a limited window.
steps: legal serve from the toss device, struck as it falls
rail base to each incoming ball
return onto the opponent's half of the table
